lore: Bai Qi, a youth from the Southlands, was gifted to the royalty of Yong to serve as an experimental weapon. After they weathered a sudden crisis together, the once-hostile relationship between him and the young sovereign of Yong blossomed into a close friendship. The two grew up side by side. As the Blood Clan invasion overflowed the borders of the Southlands, they set off to Jixia together in search of wisdom. As they journeyed, however, they were ambushed by a Blood Clan regiment. Bai Qi wrested a weapon from the hand of the enemy leader and cut a path forward for their party, but was infected by the Blood Clan in the process. The sages at Jixia were able to treat his wound, but warned that the seal they placed over it should never be broken. Otherwise, there would be no saving Bai Qi. After the two friends returned from Jixia, Yong launched an assault on the Blood Clan. Bai Qi fought without abandon. While Yong was eventually able to drive off the Blood Clan, it came at a cost—the seal over Bai Qi's wound had been broken. As the power of the Blood Clan burst forth once more, his wound festered, and Bai Qi was haunted by bloody nightmares. To save his original nature, the sovereign of Yong removed Bai Qi's mask and forced him to endure the light of the sun. With great pain, Bai Qi struggled through the most difficult days. However, he thought of how the new Yong was lacking in strength, but steadfast and hungry for justice—just like himself. He needed to become more powerful if he were to protect the nation. Thus, Bai Qi donned his mask once more, allowing himself to be infused with the power of the Blood Clan. He accepted this corruption, for one purpose alone—to gain power none could stand against.

lore:
Ancient Anomalic: The Qiao clan of Wu adhered to complex and strict traditions in order to maintain the sorcery passed down through their bloodline. But their worst fear came to pass: the birth of the first twin girls in thousands of years seemed to fulfill the prophecy that the Qiao clan would die. Terrified of what would come to pass, the elders made a cold-blooded decision: the older sister would be groomed as the heir, and the younger would be erased from the family tree and sent to Jixia.

Under her family's strict upbringing, Da Qiao became an elegant maiden, perfect in everything except her refusal to approach the ocean. To her people's displeasure, she never showed the strength they expected from an heir. Could they have made the wrong decision? Only the patriarch, her grandfather, remained stubbornly adamant. When he died, his last words, "bride of the sea", left everyone confused.

At that time, the coast was in turmoil. When the rulers of Wu learned of Da Qiao's reputation, they desired her. Having reached the end of their rope, the Qiao clan decided to offer him this beautiful yet useless tribute. Having lost her only defender, her grandfather, and with her sister out of reach in Jixia, Da Qiao agreed to sacrifice herself for the family, but on one condition—that before her wedding, she be allowed to go to the seaside and pray to her grandfather. And so, her clansmen agreed to her request.

She carried a lamp onto the rocks, in a place where the waves spoke in a way only she could understand. She listened calmly to the waves, preparing herself for what fate had in store. All she wanted was to protect the tiny light she had. It was her only hope of changing her destiny.

Neither the shroud of night nor the thick clouds could hide the faint, stubborn light, keeping the clansmen reassured that she could not escape. It was late, but at dawn, after three days of exhausting rituals, the end would come. They would send off the bride of the sea in exchange for glory for their clan.

lore:
Her name, along with those of her companions, are as old as the history of the continent. Songs and stories about them have been passed down through the ages and across the world. Their triumphs and feats are recorded in inscriptions and scrolls and have been celebrated for generations.

No one knows their past. Only a fraction of the full truth can be pieced together from mottled frescoes and untraceable folk tales.

After surviving countless trials and tribulations through immeasurable spans of time eons ago, the superbeings emerged from catastrophe and arrived in a new land.

Yet the wasteland before Nuwa's eyes was barren and lifeless. Thunderclaps were the only sounds that pierced the desolate silence, but within the earth surged a strange power...

Nuwa began to wonder if she could harness the power of the earth and—combined with her knowledge and wisdom—rebuild a new home, the beautiful home of her memories.

After innumerable failures, life upon the continent began a long and steady process of evolution. Under Nuwa's watchful gaze, new life was born.

Seeing humanity before her, Nuwa's heart overflowed with joy. It finally dawned on her that all her previous trials and tribulations had been for this moment. She had fulfilled the mission given to her by fate: to ignite the spark of hope and establish an everlasting civilization.

Nuwa and her superbeing companions passed on their knowledge to humanity bit by bit, teaching them how to survive on the planet, how to produce and create. Humans, in turn, put full trust in the superbeings, relying on them totally and earnestly accepting their care and teachings.

Using the command of creation, Nuwa built homes to shelter mankind from wind and rain and keep them safe from danger. The homes gradually coalesced to form the world's first cities.

Nuwa's knowledge and wisdom contained insights from beyond the present time, allowing her to guide the nascent human race, step by step, on its path to splendor.

Under her patient care, humans lived in peace and contentment as civilization continued to advance. As humanity flourished, Nuwa's name spread far and wide, becoming legendary in every corner of the world.

"Her mind is as vast as the sea, and her feats are as brilliant as the sun."

People sang Nuwa's praises, penned poems about her, and prayed for her blessings. Artisans painted scrolls and murals of her likeness, and her believers traveled everywhere to convey her words.

lore:
A pair of twin daughters were born to the Qiao family, a sorcerer clan of Eastbank, Jiang. But to the Qiaos, twins were seen as a bad omen, so the younger of the two was sent to be raised in Jixia. There, she grew up cheerful and carefree, perhaps because her clan had no power to control her. That girl was Xiao Qiao.

Having grown into a young woman, Xiao Qiao was brought back home. Long accustomed to being free and unrestrained, Xiao Qiao was different from those around her: compassionate, unrealistically optimistic, and perhaps naive. But what made her even more different was the powerful magic she possessed—and this made others fear her. Xiao Qiao could use sophisticated sorcery with ease. It was a natural talent in her blood, requiring neither guidance nor practice. Her clan was frightened by this power and decided to send her to live out her remaining days in a village near the sea.

Not long after, a strange illness began to spread along the coast. Blockaded within the village and terrified of the inexplicable disease, the citizens attacked the soldiers stationed there, and the scene descended into chaos. The one who received orders to quell this commotion was none other than Zhou Yu.

Keenly perceptive, Xiao Qiao realized that the movement of air was a factor in the spread of the illness, so she tried to use the power of wind to drive away the infected air that was making people sick. Seeing Xiao Qiao calmly casting spells amidst the panic, Zhou Yu misunderstood her magic as the malignant cause of the crisis and took her into custody as a suspect.

Their first encounter took place in a dilapidated dungeon, in which Xiao Qiao stubbornly did her best to persuade the handsome officer. It took a full night of questioning for Zhou Yu to come to believe Xiao Qiao's airborne contagion theory, while Xiao Qiao had fallen head-over-heels in love with the man at first sight... The cooperation between the two saved many lives, while in the process, Zhou Yu learned of certain rumors about the Blood Clan and was alerted to a hidden crisis on the sea hundreds of miles away... When the illness finally subsided after a few months and Zhou Yu decided to return to Jiang, he found himself unable to leave Xiao Qiao there all alone. In his life, which was so burdened with responsibility, Xiao Qiao was like a glittering star that lit up the gloomy seas of his heart.

The entire world knows that Zhou Yu, the Ironwilled, is hard-nosed and firm-willed. No one can shake him. But within his rigid and rigorous soldierly life, Xiao Qiao is the only accident that ever slipped through the cracks. "Love and war both require bravery."

lore:
The ancient era produced a glorious civilization, and one of its greatest achievements was that of arcane machinery. However, the mysteries of the mechanical arts had been lost to time. No one expected that the mechanical arts would be revived at the hands of an ordinary craftsman.

Previously, Fuzi had wanted to set up a school to pass on his knowledge, and he received generous donations from the imperial family to establish Jixia Academy. Among the craftsmen enlisted in the academy's construction was a youth named Mo Di, who spent the next thirty years exploring every corner of Jixia, including the ruins of an ancient city buried underground. It was a city built by ancient sages, and home to the Tower of Enlightenment. Guided by his natural talent, Mo Di quickly grasped the hidden principles of the forgotten machinery and began experimenting. Aided by his mechanical inventions, known as "Mohist Machinery", Jixia Academy built ample facilities, including the famous "Mozi Arena," for talented students from around the world to come and practice their skills. As the academy attracted numerous other mechanical experts, the art was successfully salvaged from the past.

Mo Di soon became one of the Three Sages of Jixia Academy, and was given the honorary name "Mozi". He then accomplished the greatest feat of his life—the construction of Chang'an, a thriving city located in the center of the continent. The product of Mozi's tireless toil and deep wisdom, the city became known as the greatest wonder since ancient times. Chang'an boasted unprecedented prosperity, serving as inspiration for poets and bards—and a target of envy from other rulers.

However, the flourishing of Chang'an attracted the covetous gazes of many ambitious people, so the city was home to continuous conflict and strife until the empire was securely established. Much to Mozi's indignation, the serpentine walls and embattlements protecting Chang'an were subject to repeated attacks by massive siege engines of all kinds. This enraged Mozi, fueling his passion to push the boundaries of mechanical invention and prevent the fruits of his labor from being destroyed.

lore:
There was a time as the ancient era drew to a close when the Continent was thrown into chaos. Only three regions in the east were spared the fires of war and continued to flourish. Guided by the culture passed down to them from Jixia, the three regions enriched themselves by different means: Wei specialized in forging iron, Shu was skilled in the arts of machinery, and Wu excelled at shipbuilding.

The Eastern Sea and long ocean voyages brought wealth and prosperity to Wu. Ships were the lifeblood of Wu, and those who controlled this lifeblood became rich and powerful. They monopolized ships and navigation routes. Content to lord over their small section of the world, they were obsessed with pleasure and searching for a way to extend their lives, unconcerned that Wu was falling apart. Zhou Yu was born to one of these leading families. A single question burned in his heart: "What kind of country will Wu become?"

Determined to find the answer to this question, Zhou Yu made the long journey to study at Jixia Academy. Fuzi's teaching gave him no direct answer. He and his fellow students debated day and night, searching for a theory, a method to bring lasting peace and order to Primaera.

In these debates, he always met his match in one student — Kongming.

While he could never beat Kongming in debate, Zhou Yu was convinced that his own ideas were correct. His opponent's empty, theoretical arguments reinforced his conviction that the ideal country could be built only through action.

So when Sun Ce invited him to return to Wu to build that ideal country, he went without a second thought.

Zhou Yu hoped to squash the pirates who had been tormenting the people. The land could only be at peace when the people did not live in fear of calamity.

When that day came, Wu would become the land of his dreams—a country of order and peace.

On the path to this ideal, he would have to face those who held absolute power: the aristocracy. Zhou Yu aided Sun Ce in amassing power and building an armored fleet. Their ships, while few in number, had powerful armaments. Against the tides and into the wind, they set sail for Jiang.

When asked about the most legendary musician on the continent, people always bring up Gao.

A talented musician, he had the world enamored with his astonishing skills and wild personality from his first public performance—especially the girls. At the height of his fame, he would hold banquets every night, spending the inordinate amounts of the money he was easily earning and surrounding himself with beautiful people.

However, this life of debauchery was unable to bring Gao long-term happiness, and over time he began to feel a terrible emptiness in his heart. When wealth and status come too easily, there's no regret in giving them up. And so just as fast as it appeared, the name "Gao" faded from people's minds.

Gao carried his beloved lute on his back and traveled across the continent. He went to the seaside and listened to the sound of the waves, he climbed up mountains and listened to the melody of the wind in the trees, and these experiences took his music to the next level. He can manipulate every string and every note to his heart's desire, and not only is he able to please people with his music, but he can also play deadly tones that seriously wound his enemies.

One day during his travels, Gao found himself on a battlefield. As he hid and waited for the battle to end, he witnessed a scene that would go on to change his fate. A never-before-seen monster appeared in the Yong Army, claiming hundreds of lives. This was Bai Qi, also known as the "ultimate weapon."

In a moment of complete shock, Gao realized he had found a higher calling, one that surpassed even music: stopping war.

After leaving the battlefield, he started contacting people who had the same goal, and in the process ended up meeting a prince. He attended one of the prince's banquets, serving as a musician. It just so happened to be the same banquet where a female assassin came to kill the prince, but she was seriously injured and fell into a coma.

Dr. Bian had been living with his mentor, Xu Fu, since he could remember. He was once an innocent youth who studied medicine with a passion to save the world. Dr. Bian always felt extremely proud whenever he saw a patient recovering because of his treatment. However, never in those days did Dr. Bian notice how his mentor, Xu Fu, was suspiciously covering his tracks, nor did he notice the vigilance and fear that flashed through his mentor's eyes. Until one seemingly ordinary day, his mentor left with the first-aid kit to visit a patient and never came back.

Dr. Bian was forced to start seeing patients on his own, and he saved countless lives with his excellent medical skills. While passing through Jixia, Dr. Bian learned of an ancient medical technique, one capable of regenerating an injured body, making an aged face youthful again. The people vaguely regarded this inconceivable technique as a part of "sorcery", and it was a taboo that they were unwilling to talk about. As Dr. Bian's reputation as a "divine doctor" spread, the Sovereign of Yong sought his treatment too. But the man who actually met Dr. Bian was his long-lost mentor, Xu Fu, who was now Queen Mother Mi Yue's most trusted royal physician.

Dr. Bian cured the Sovereign of Yong successfully, but Xu Fu requested that Dr. Bian stay behind to help him with secret surgical experiments that involved sorcery. The unsuspecting Dr. Bian agreed to his mentor's request. However, as soon as the surgery was over, Xu Fu tore off the mask of kindness he'd been wearing. The Sovereign of Yong was poisoned to death, and Dr. Bian was arrested as the culprit. Only now did Dr. Bian realize that he'd been framed by the person he trusted the most.

In his moment of desperation, Dr. Bian recalled the surgery's anesthetics that were hidden between the layers of his sash. Dr. Bian was able to seize an opportunity to drug the jailer and escape Yong. But his mentor had no intention of letting him escape. Assassins caught up to Dr. Bian near Jixia, and they dug open a huge hole and buried him alive. Dr. Bian collapsed into a pit of despair. He thought death was upon him. But a sudden rainstorm washed away the rocks, and as the cliff collapsed, Dr. Bian broke free from the grasps of the soil and fell into the darkness below.

lore:
Beauty once changed Mi Yue's destiny.

Mi Yue would never forget the admiration and astonishment in the Sovereign of Yong's eyes when he saw her for the first time, and it marked the end of her humble life as an adolescent girl. She relied upon her tactical insight and weaponized her beauty in order to not only survive amid the numerous concubines, but eventually become Yong's Empress Dowager.

But time is fair, and it shows pity to no one. When her youth escaped her like sand escaping between the fingers, and as the young emperor approached adulthood, Mi Yue realized that the authority and prestige she possessed were like a candle in the wind, they may be extinguished at any moment. Mi Yue began succumbing deeper into anxiety and fear, day by day.

During this time, a man who called himself Xu Fu came to kneel, trembling, before her, anxiously and desperately seeking her protection. The tribute he presented her was a potion for eternal youth.

Mi Yue consumed the potion and had a wonderful dream that night. In her dream, she was back in her youth when her beauty was at its prime, and she was looking down upon her enemies of the past. Once she awoke, Mi Yue realized that the dream wasn't just a dream. She saw herself from 20 years ago in the mirror. Just as Xu Fu had said, her lost youth and beauty were hers again.

Xu Fu got his wish. Mi Yue named him the royal physician, and he received the protection he desired. Mi Yue gave Xu Fu a special medical chamber so that he may brew more of that rare potion.

In the days that followed, Xu Fu kept requesting materials for the potion, and for the sake of those potions, Mi Yue even started raising feralis.

However, the duration of the potion's effects was growing increasingly shorter.

When faced with an impatient Mi Yue and her questions, Xu Fu presented her another secret recipe—A potion of longevity! Mi Yue learned of the glorious ancient times, and the people of those times who relied on sorcery to possess longer-lasting life and youth.

lore:
Lady Zhen was a great beauty, renowned across the continent for her gentleness and benevolence. Born into a noble family, she carried the bloodline of an ancient sage, for which everyone in Primaera revered her. From a young age, she was raised to shoulder her responsibilities, restrain her desires, and toil selflessly to purify the world of corruption.

But after eighteen years of perseverance, all her cautious discretion was shattered upon meeting that man. His youthful face, bold and fearless action, his intense ambition, his heart-stopping honeyed words—They all left her head spinning.

"The meaning of my life has only been to meet you."

"May the lady accept my praise: You are as beautiful as the moonlit clouds, as charming as the drifting snow."

"Graceful as a startled swan, and kind as a benevolent spirit."

Lady Zhen's heart, as placid as the surface of a calm lake, rippled for the first time with the desire to break free from the shackles of her identity. For once, she wanted to take hold of her own destiny.

Though it caused her great hardship, she eventually abandoned her family, her fate, and her nobility. She had finally fulfilled her desire: to marry into the Cao family, which was rising rapidly in power.

However, the man who stood before her on their wedding night was familiar yet not at the same time. While he had once been an affectionate partner, now it was as if he had two faces—one a dashing young gentleman, and the other a savagely ambitious heir.

Lady Zhen realized that she had fallen into a trap: The Cao clan had sought her not for her beauty, but for the power she had inherited through her bloodline.

lore:
A married couple, both poor artisans from the Riverlands, Gan Jiang and his wife, Mo Ye, had been childhood sweethearts and had always depended on each other for survival. Gan Jiang had no outstanding talents and was only interested in forging swords, but Mo Ye supported him without reservation.

Only knowing how to forge swords, Gan Jiang felt guilty. He had hoped to make a name for himself and give his wife a better life, so he visited swordsmiths all over the land, smashing up their countless masterpieces, and soon his name spread across the Misty Marshes. Of course, the swordsmiths he'd vandalized hated his guts.

There was only one master swordsmith in the world. People said the swords he forged were not only sharp, but also had a soul within them. Gan Jiang had attacked many of this master's disciples, and after they complained to him, the master decided to invite Gan Jiang for a visit. He wasn't just any master: He was truly the most outstanding swordsmith alive. But when Gan Jiang arrived, the master didn't show up. Instead, he ordered his disciples to greet Gan Jiang with swords, and so the master's swords clashed with Gan Jiang's. The artisan roared! They laughed at him, repaying him with double the humiliation he had dished out.

Gan Jiang fled with failure burning in his heart. He returned home and recommenced his dull life of forging. His furnace never stopped burning, and every sword was sharper than the last, but they were still lifeless pieces of iron. The difference between a dead sword and a living sword is as great as the difference between heaven and earth. Gan Jiang became obsessed with forging swords, completely forgetting his original purpose, so he was oblivious to the fact that his wife was growing weak and frail.

lore:
"Those who shoulder the burden of fate keep going even when alone."

In ancient times, humans lived in brutal and barren lands. Savage feralis roamed everywhere, forcing humanity to retreat into impossible places. Two great sages, Ziya and Fuzi, left their tribe behind in their 50s and set out to find a better way for humans to survive, embarking on a pilgrimage called the "Journey of Divinity".

After thirty long years of arduous ordeals, they finally arrived at the destination appointed by the superbeings, haggard and worn out by the journey. Nuwa granted them the title of "Enforcers"—the first of their kind.

When Nuwa inquired as to why they wished to become Enforcers, they only replied, "For our people." When they returned to their tribe, however, they discovered that most of the people who had seen them off had already passed away. The ones who remained had been children, still learning to speak, at the time of the sages' departure.

The sages delivered the knowledge of the superbeings to humanity, leading them out of barbarity so that they might stand on their own. Next, the sages endured the Ferali War together, during which the Enforcers suffered heavy losses. By then, years had passed, and humanity had grown strong. So, Nuwa ordered Ziya to select outstanding humans to take over the mantle as new Enforcers. Meanwhile, Fuzi had displayed the greatest martial skill of all Enforcers during the war, so he was gifted the Ferule of Superbeings, also known as "Vigilance." As the Enforcer of Precepts and on behalf of the superbeings, Fuzi guarded the mortal code of conduct and ensured peace in the human world.

Later on, during a great war known as the Fall of the Superbeings, the two sages fought as Enforcers under Nuwa. Though both sides paid a heavy price in lives, when the dust settled, the Dark Master Diqun had been defeated. After the Fall, the remaining Enforcers and superbeings dispersed. Nuwa entrusted Fuzi and Ziya with the duties of guarding humanity and guiding its path, but over time, it became evident that the two sages had differing views on how the human race should progress—differences that eventually caused them to part ways.

lore:
Mercenaries are common during chaotic times. And this is the story of a mercenary in a powerful group led by someone called "Dragon."

Diaochan was one of the few women in the group, flitting between different factions as the peerless dancer. When her body moved, she wove tender dreams that captivated everyone around her. She was the only one awake in these dreams, and she stole information or killed her targets as Dragon commanded. Diaochan told herself that the admiration and infatuation others showered her with were just dreams, and she must always stay awake if she wanted to survive in this world.

Diaochan's next order was to approach and kill Lu Bu, the Warlord. He was the crucial last obstacle in Dragon's journey to be free from his mercenary identity and become someone truly powerful. Diaochan gained Lu Bu's trust through her whispered words of false love, and the brutal warlord fell willingly into the beautiful dream she'd woven. On the eve of the fight against the mercenaries, it fell on her to keep Lu Bu's cup full. One of the many times she came over to fill it, Lu Bu held onto her wrist. "Just you wait. You will have the world on a platter tomorrow..." Was the brutal Warlord Lu Bu giving her his heart? Diaochan's joy and admiration almost fooled herself. Sincerity was useless when it came to survival.

The Crescent Halberd cut Lu Bu's hand, and his blood dripped into the cup. Dragon accepted this cup in the shadowed corner of a tent. "With this... sorcery, even the Warlord cannot stop me. Just you wait. Tomorrow..."

The sun rose and fell just the same, but things were different. The battlefield smelled faintly of fragrance as the silhouette of a woman darted through it. Not Diaochan the dancer, but Diaochan the scout, looking for her companions while the soldiers fled.

Were they dead? Were they... all dead? Was Lu Bu truly invincible? Were her tricks useless against his absolute power?

lore:
The Chonokh tribes once roamed the vast grasslands of the continent's northern reaches. There, they lived off the land, shepherding their livestock. Chonokh men and women alike served as fierce warriors, accompanied by packs of wolves.

As bitter cold invaded from the north froze the grasslands, the tribes were forced to migrate southward, launching attack after attack upon the Central Plains.

The nations of the Central Plains had been at war with one another, but when faced with the repeated attacks of the fierce warriors, their leaders had no choice but to present a united front and negotiate with the Chonokh. A temporary truce was reached at great cost in grain and cloth, and along with these gifts of peace came a Central Plains princess — Wang Zhaojun.

The Chonokh took the princess to their sacred place, the Winter Ocean, where they offered her up as a bride to their tribal deity. They believed that doing so would prompt the deity to descend upon the world and protect the tribes. Over time, this tradition had evolved into a sacred yet cruel ritual—and the princess' life was tribute.

Wang Zhaojun's body lay trapped in ice for years while the continent was embroiled in war. Several powerful nations arose from the ruins of war, and they no longer wished to honor the truce with the Chonokh. These nations made plans to exterminate the northern barbarians.

They hatched a savage plot: to attack the plains while the tribes were celebrating a wedding, a time when the Chonokh would be totally unprepared to defend themselves. The verdant grasslands were stained crimson that day. Later histories would record the event as the "Red Wedding."

Even so, the generals were not satisfied with the slaughter. They sought the treasures hidden away in the icy tundra, in the glacial resting place of the sacrificed brides where troves of valuables placed as offerings to the tribal deity lay frozen.

The butchers got exactly what they wanted. They cheered as they began hauling crates of gold back toward the Central Plains. But before they knew it, the sky turned dark and a blizzard descended out of nowhere, followed by a torrential avalanche.

Dangerous magic slumbered in a dilapidated temple, where an old man named Jiang Ziya lived. To find a suitable disciple to accomplish his goal, he carefully picked several of the most talented people in the world and taught them sorcery at the temple.

Liang was among the chosen, and the most unique of the lot. He never learned any of the existing sorcery from Jiang Ziya, but instead created his own version, which he called Power Word.

With the strength of Power Word, Liang broke the barrier between languages, mastering almost every language spoken by humans. In his ears, the voices of every living being were one. By extension, he could talk to the land and even communicate with the world, and this took him closer to the truth than anyone had ever been. To him, common sorcery was child's play.

Even Jiang Ziya trembled at Liang's strength, and Liang saw endless possibilities.

Since he had a better understanding of the world than anyone else, he was no longer an ordinary human. If he wanted to, he could become a deity.

"Perhaps this disciple of mine could restore order to this world," thought Jiang Ziya, so he explained his vision for the world to Liang.

Then Liang traveled back into the world and was immediately confronted with a Misty Marshes divided by conflict. He also encountered Liu Bang and Xiang Yu.

Was Xiang Yu, the rising youth, the reincarnated Dark Master as predicted by his teacher?

Liang expected his biggest obstacles to be brutal battles or treacherous manipulations, but he was wrong: It turned out to be simple survival.

Though peonies bloomed magnificently from the city down to the river, it is said that only Yuhuan and her music can match up to this breathtaking view. Both beauty and melodies were the crown jewels of Chang'an, and the fact that no one seems to know where the mysterious Yuhuan had come from only added to her allure. Rumor had it that the first time she leaned out of her veranda to gaze at the moon and play her music, affluent young men swarmed from all over the city to try and catch a glimpse of her. It was even claimed that the number of disturbances reported in Changle District rose as a result.

One day a year, during the Shangsi Festival, crowds flocked to the river to try and see this beauty for themselves. The sound of her pipa was like flowing water, for it poured out the tunes of her heart. The beauty from the north had charmed the entire city... no, the entire kingdom. She had come to Chang'an to show her talents to the world and seek her own happiness.

The merchants coming from the west would listen to her stories. Her music tugged at their heartstrings, and they'd begin to recall the desert forts and cities of years gone by. The strange thing was, as her stirring music played, the ruins seemed to slowly reform, like a mirage at sea.

The people of Chang'an also listened to her music. But oddly, the same music painted wholly different scenes in front of their eyes: morning bells and evening drums rang all over Chang'an City, and the whole city was shining brightly, as if not of this earthly world.

The magistrate among the folk became puzzled. "Is the sound of the pipa meant to confound me?" He asked. No, there was no sign of wavering in my mind, though I could really feel from the music a most beautiful age of prosperity for Chang'an which I've dreamed of day and night.

The sound of music could be heard in the elegant courtyard not far from Changle Hall. Yixing stopped mid-game, Weiqi stone in hand. Pei looked up abruptly. The Peony Diviner remained unmoved and continued to focus on his peonies. The dancer, however, could not help but start moving lightly on her feet.

"No matter how many times I hear Yuhuan's lute, I'm always moved by it. Why doesn't my dance have the same effect?"

"Because the music makes you hear what you long for."

Even during his days as a pupil, Kongming was already regarded as the most gifted student in Jixia Academy's history, possessing truly exceptional intelligence and talent. Recognized as the successor to Fuzi himself, Kongming ranked first in all examinations, whether in sorcery, machinery, wisdom, or the art of war.

Yet Kongming cared nothing for such admiration and praise, instead focusing his efforts on the study of ancient knowledge. In the course of his research, he discovered that the origin, growth, destruction, and rebirth of Primaera were all closely linked to something that had once existed: the "origin of knowledge." The superbeings who had created civilization and built the Wonders had also made contact with the origin of knowledge, but after they exited the stage of human history, no one had made contact with it since.

As a youth, Kongming traveled to every corner of the continent in search of the origin of knowledge. He visited the ancient ruins beneath Jixia to make copies of ancient texts, and before leaving, he placed a magical ward to seal off the ruins from any would-be thieves. He had held in his hands Chang'an's greatest secret, and had journeyed to the ancient kingdom that had vanished amidst the desert sands...

He shuttled back and forth from one ancient ruin to the next, gathering wisdom and knowledge from all reaches of time and space.

Finally, he decided to settle in the kingdom of Shu to focus on analyzing all the information he had collected. Kongming's precious knowledge had always attracted the attention of unseemly characters. It is said that once, Zilong, the "Dragonshadow Spear," had visited Kongming's hut, intending to steal his collection. However, after approaching the cottage, Zilong was never seen again.

Among the many guests who came to visit Kongming, only Liu Bei, a member of the imperial family, was allowed to enjoy a cup of tea with him. Liu Bei requested Kongming's help in governing the kingdom, but Kongming refused. In his eyes, political concerns paled in comparison to exploring the mystery of the origin of knowledge.

The knowledge left behind by the superbeings was like a double-edged blade: sooner or later, it would be used for evil. Through his research, Kongming realized that dark forces were at play, manipulating the origin of knowledge to influence the course of history. He focused every bit of his powerful intellect, attempting to uncover the truth that had been hidden from mankind—a truth that just might turn the world upside down.

lore:
"The world is too painful. What can I do to forget about it?"

"Play Weiqi."

"Weiqi? Can that really replace the world?"

"Yes. These nineteen rows and columns hold a universe all of their own."

The boy, covered in injuries, picked up a white stone and placed it squarely in the center of the board, just like his father whom he had secretly watched before. The world has been cruel, but he had no wish to be beaten down. He was a human being, and he longed for the happiness he deserved, but all he could do was confine his thoughts and feelings within the world of the Weiqi board.

Time flew like an arrow. As spring arrived and the flowers bloomed, the boy made his appearance before the people of Chang'an with his benefactor, the Peony Diviner, who had saved his life and taught him how to play Weiqi.

An emissary had come from Kyokutou and managed to obtain an audience with the Empress, when he produced a Weiqi set made of jade and asked to play against the best players of Chang'an. The emissary was surprisingly skilled, and beat several masters in a row. The smile on the Empress's face slowly faded.

Just as the court officials were cowering from the heat of the Empress's rage, the Peony Diviner suggested that the young man play against the emissary. Everyone looked at the small figure in disbelief. Had they known that this would be the first time that the young man played against a real opponent, they'd probably have been even more taken aback.

The emissary from Kyokutou looked at the trembling, young man sitting in front of the Weiqi board with disdain. "Ha!" He thought. "He probably hasn't even been weaned from his mother's bosom yet!" But this contempt soon disappeared in the face of a series of bold and sophisticated moves.

lore:
South of Sunset, the ruling clans built a great city—Navenia. The ruler of Navenia was given the title 'Mecha Commander', and the Mecha Commander of the current generation is Milady. Generation after generation, Mecha Commanders have held the power to keep the city running and prospering. It's said that this power originated from long ago in the ancient world, when knowledge and wisdom began.

This power was passed down from one generation to another, keeping Navenia orderly, and thriving. When Milady became ruler of Navenia, she took control of this great and wondrous power.

To the outside world, Milady is a refined noble—a cold and determined lady who brooked no argument. Only Milady knows what terrible price her ancestors paid for their miraculous powers—an unrelenting curse.

Beneath Milady's long elegant gloves, something strange is happening to her body—crystallization. Starting from the tips of her fingers, little by little, her palms are becoming hard and transparent. Even the city isn't immune to this corruption. There are subtle but continuous changes—polluted water, corrosion, and crystallization... and she desperately wants to break the curse.

Coincidentally, there was a businessman called Niccolo Polo in Navenia who was very interested in machines, and was a student of a famous mechanics master. During one of his business trips, Niccolo Polo happened to come across a record describing the art of machinery and the origins of knowledge.

Though he sent the files back to Navenia, they were personally destroyed by his master.

Upon learning that the way to break the curse had been destroyed, Milady became enraged and imprisoned the master with her Mechanical Minion. Later, she held the master and Niccolo Polo's only son captive, demanding that Niccolo Polo find the way to break the curse again.

Niccolo Polo set out once more. But this time, he vanished into the far east, never to return.

Fifteen years later, the consul's mansion posted a notice looking to recruit fearless adventurers to venture to the far reaches of the continent. A young trader, Marco Polo, Niccolo Polo's only son, signed up. After bidding farewell to the master who had been teaching him, he ventured east in search of his father, aided by the notes that his father had left behind.

lore:
Buds bloom in an instant, blossoming into charming peonies. Curious, the little girl stretches out her fingertips, but as soon as she touches them, their petals wither and transform into a black mist that envelops her, attempting to pull her into the endless abyss. The girl screams and struggles to break free, until...

She suddenly jolted awake. The girl's heart continued to beat rapidly. It was the same horrible nightmare again. She had been tortured by this recurring nightmare since she was three years old. She had always had a hunch that there was a secret hidden in the nightmare, closely related to a distant memory long buried and forgotten.

The Royal Library not only houses precious books from all over the world but also stores numerous calligraphy and painted scrolls by famous artists. The ones who looked after the library are maidservants who has been condemned for crimes in court. Among them was a girl named Shangguan.

Shangguan's grandfather was originally an official who the previous emperor had assigned to the deposed prince as a tutor. Unexpectedly, the old man ended up being swept up in the prince's attempted rebellion, which caused his family to be punished. The men were sent to join the army, and the women were sent to the palace as servants. Shangguan was only four years old when she entered the palace. Now, many years later, her relatives had gradually departed, leaving her to grow up alone. Despite her burdensome work in the library, she managed to practice calligraphy every day. This was the only thing she had left of her grandfather, a famous calligrapher.

When the Empress' birthday arrived, someone recommended a great painter to capture her likeness. As she was busy with her affairs, she ordered the painter to live in the palace library, to facilitate his work. The great painter thus spent half of his time following the empress to capture sketches, and the other half buried in the library, creating his painting. The library official assigned the clever Shangguan to assist the painter.

The great painter was a knowledgeable, humorous, and interesting individual who had traveled to many places. Not only were his portraits lifelike, he could also beautifully capture landscapes and scenes he had encountered with just a few strokes. Shangguan was very envious; she had not once left the palace since the age of four. How fascinating it was to see the outside world through his masterful brush.

"If you haven't seen the world, if you haven't witnessed human joy, anger, sorrow, and desire, then your brush will only ever depict the surface of things. The same is true for painting and writing alike. And yes, I am talking about your writing."

The Southlands, also known as the Desolate Lands, is hardly a childhood paradise. Shi learned various survival tricks from a young age. Her first attempt to trade treasure she found resulted in her incurring a huge debt. While fleeing her pursuers, she stumbled into an ancient shrine dedicated to a goddess. There, she found a magical silk ribbon.

Originating from the distant and mysterious southern continent, this ribbon was closely related to her clan. Its power protected her many times over the following years, but it also attracted some who coveted it. Disguising themselves as debtors, they pursued her relentlessly and meticulously lured her into a trap. Unaware of what was truly happening, Shi was saved by Zhuangzi and took refuge in Jixia, where she assumed a new identity. She studied sorcery and participated in various tournaments, hoping to clear her debts so that she could wander the world like her teacher Zhuangzi.

Despite what she learned from her hardships in the Southlands, Shi had never understood what true "treasure" was. That was, until she faced the challenges alongside the Team of Stars in the Dream Trial. Through her teammates' choices, she finally grasped the real meaning of treasure. This signified the start of a new life for this treasure hunter.

lore:
Upon your return to Jixia after studying abroad, some inexplicable things began happening to you. It started with magic surging through you and accidentally destroying the dorm's tea table, taking an entire month of living expenses with it. After that, when Luban's mechcraft parts fell from above, your body moved on instinct. In a flash, the bracelet on your wrist transformed into a shield as you charged forward to block the fall, destroying the windows of the teaching building in the process.

Incidents like these were too numerous to count. At the slightest thought, different weapons would emerge from your bracelet, and the moment they landed in your hands, your body would instinctively respond with perfect precision. Both sorcery and martial arts just came naturally to you, as if imprinted within you, despite your certainty that you'd never trained in any of it. You didn't know where the weapons came from, nor where you'd learned these moves that seemed to land you in constant trouble. But despite how unfamiliar it all felt... there was something oddly familiar about it too.

Even in Jixia Academy, where talent abounds, this was far from common. Not to mention you have no idea how this all came to be. Your enrolment into Jixia Academy remains clear in your memories, even Fuzi's friendly suggestion that led to you studying abroad... But what happened after that? Racking your brains for answers only ends with splitting headaches.

Headmaster Fuzi seems to know something, yet refuses to say much. It makes you feel uneasy. But for the sake of the truth, you decide to go along with Fuzi's advice and find your own truth in battle.

The Fate Clan had been away from the Navenian Council for so long, the people of Navenia may have forgotten what they used to be like.

There was a time when the Fate Clan was one of the leading clans of Navenia who steered the kingdom with their ability to see the future.

However, the ones who led the way met with sudden misfortune and were lost to the Deep Sea, and the stars have dimmed since then.

When Heino was a child, the Scepter of Fate predicted that the Fate Clan was destined to fall. As a result, it was said by some that Heino was the ominous portent signalling the clan's downfall.

If the fall of the clan was the likeliest possibility that an infinite future held, then Heino had been on the road to fighting fate alone ever since he had become the head of the clan as a young boy.

Despite opposition from the rest of his clan, Heino made the decision to relocate Revelation Hall to the outskirts of the city to be more in touch with the common people and build prestige for the Fate Clan. In the face of competition from the other clans, he gave up most of their assets apart from a well-run restaurant and opera house which would serve as the clan's lifeline.

Through this, he was able to save the Fate Clan from extinction, unlike the other Arkana clans.

It was only then that everyone realized that the one with the so-called bad luck was actually the one they could trust and rely on the most.

"I don't believe our fates are set in stone."

"Fate" has never been about shackles that we can't escape. It is not the end, but the path we forge through in life.

"Seeing thousands of possible fates as I walk the path of infinities." Heino firmly believes that outcomes can be reversed, and is determined to make the light of fate shine bright again.

lore:
The Golden City was one of the earliest Alsahraa kingdoms to rise. After it conquered the other kingdoms in a war, Alsahraa enjoyed a short-lived period of peace and prosperity. The kingdom eventually fell to the Iron Riders from Chang'an, and both the king and the queen perished. The royal family led their people elsewhere to establish another kingdom, while those from Chang'an took over the old capital and built Dunefort.

Gao Changgong was supposed to grow up to become a respectable ruler and carry on the legacies of the previous kings. However, after witnessing his parents leap to their deaths from the spire as the troops from Central Plains breached the city wall, and then seeing Dunefort built on the ruins of his beloved city, the seed of hatred was sown in his heart. He decided to take back the lost land and exact revenge on Dunefort as well as the Great Wall.

A mysterious hermit from the mountains took Gao Changgong away and trained him to become an assassin.

The once-noble prince became a killer in the shadows. He was hired by powerful people many times to assassinate peace envoys, leading to clashes, suspicion, and fear.

The kingdom that was supposed to be his had become a wasteland, and the forgotten land was buried under ruins. But Gao Changgong never gave up on his revenge.

An impenetrable and colossal obstacle stood between him and his goal: the Great Wall. As long as it stood, the eastern empire would not fall. To take back what was his, he must destroy Dunefort, which stood above the old capital, as well as the Great Wall.

But since the Great Wall was under the watchful eyes of the Great Wall Guardians around the clock, they had to be taken down first before the Wall could be breached.

The prince scaled the Great Wall repeatedly to discover its secrets. He learned every guardian's name and hometown, the factions they belonged to, and the conflicts between the factions. He patiently searched for weaknesses in their defense and sowed the seeds of discord at the right time, just as he did during his assassinations.

lore:
Since ancient times, the mysterious Jing clan of assassins has operated under cover of night. Through countless generations, they have passed down their lethal secret sword techniques and used them to extract hefty sums from anyone wealthy enough to pay for their blades—and their silence.

The last inheritors of this clan were a lone pair of siblings, a brother and a sister. The older brother, who had inherited the assassin's alias Jing Ke, spent his days loitering in the streets with the local scoundrels, but as soon as night fell, he carried out the family trade with deadly efficiency.

However, things would change when General Fan Wuji of Qin was forced to flee to the kingdom of Yan after discovering his king's secret. Before long, his fame became a source of envy for Crown Prince Dan. "A vagrant has replaced me as the leader of the anti-Qin coalition? I will not have it!" Crown Prince Dan's men promptly brought a generous offering of gold coins to the assassin known as Jing Ke, requesting his services.

But for the first time, Jing Ke hesitated. The forthright Fan Wuji was like a brother to him, a friendship that transcended social status. In the end, Jing Ke refused the assignment.

The next day, Fan Wuji came to visit Jing Ke. He had brought with him a wooden scroll with a map of the Qin Royal Palace carved into it. He told his friend his plan—he wished to hire the Jing clan to assassinate the king of Qin, not knowing that the man standing in front of him was the very assassin that he sought to hire. Before Jing Ke could say anything, he realized that Fan Wuji had been followed. When he opened the door, they were surrounded by Crown Prince Dan's personal troops.

"It's a shame, really. I never had a chance to fight for my own sake." Jing Ke raised his blade and walked toward his ruthless opponents. In these final moments, he thought about his little sister. The fate of the entire clan would now rest on her young shoulders.

lore:
Han Xin is by nature an uncompromising strategist.

Everyone in the Misty Marshes knew that Liu Bang, to whom Han Xin was loyal, would pay any price to get what he wanted, and that he regarded his own interests as more important than anything else. However, few people knew that Han Xin's ambition was on par with, if not greater than, Liu Bang's. No matter the situation, Han Xin would always do that which benefited him.

For Han Xin, survival was difficult, but his will to live was strong. In order to survive and achieve his goals, he chose to endure humiliation. This wasn't something he accepted reluctantly, it was a choice he made.

Therefore, when a young ruffian raised his sword to humiliate Han Xin, he chose to crawl pathetically between the ruffian's legs. When an even more powerful leader appeared, he submitted and willingly shackled himself.

He didn't just endure it blindly; he was biding his time until a single strike was all he needed.

Before he became a well-known man of power and brilliant strategist, Han Xin had been brewing up a storm. A storm that would rip across the continent and inscribe his name in the annals of history.

He doesn't believe in destiny. He only believes in himself.

His long-awaited moment finally arrived. Liu Bang, who Han Xin was loyal to, was about to head into his final battle with Xiang Yu, the Dark Master who was yet to awaken. Han Xin hatched an ingenious plan and weaved a carefully constructed web.

He used an illusion to disguise himself as Consort Yu's fellow disciple, Liang, to get close to Consort Yu. He told her the cruel truth: that her sweetheart Xiang Yu was actually the Dark Master who would threaten the entire continent, and the one that she had sworn to defeat. Han Xin took advantage of her state of shock and bewitched her consciousness.

That night, when Xiang Yu was besieged by enemies and engaged in battle, Consort Yu walked out of the enemy camp like a beautiful puppet, firing an arrow that pierced his heart. Han Xin had used Consort Yu to defeat Xiang Yu.

lore:
The majestic Chang'an has stood for hundreds of years. The gate of Chang'an City, however, the impregnable Phoenix Gate, was engraved with a poem slashed into the stone by a young man with a longsword: "My heart yearns for the blue sky and to embrace the bright moon," and it caused a sensation throughout Chang'an. When magistrate Di Renjie volunteered to arrest him for vandalizing the city, the Empress refused his offer and even ordered that the Will of the Sword poem be preserved. In just a few days, the name of the young swordsman had spread throughout Chang'an City. His name was Li Bai.

At that time, Li Bai was young and frivolous. After refusing the Empress' invitation to become an official, he began a journey to hone his swordsmanship. When he saw the surging Yellow River for the first time, the Will of the Sword burst forth from within him, rushing to the sea, never to return.

With no machinery knowledge, sorcery techniques, or Ferali blood, Li Bai nevertheless became one of the greatest in the empire, relying only on himself and his sword. He was a rare natural talent. He composed a poem for each opponent he defeated, and each poem's name spread far and wide along with the name of his sword. Later, some even sought defeat at his hands in order to be honored by one of his poems—a startling turn of events.

lore:
As the High Priest, Augran is feared by all. But as Qi, he bears his mission alone.

When he was a child, Qi lived with his grandmother in the Forest Temple. Later, he set out to save Dyadia, a girl who had been displaced by the Wilting. Since then, the two stuck together, and vowed to join the Order of the Seers and protect the forest. But then the Wilting struck again, wiping out his grandma's Forest Temple.

After that, he was taken in by his master. Working hard to join the Order of the Seers, he carried his and Dyadia's oath with him.

With every strike of his spear, every incantation, and every spirit returned to its eternal resting place, another piece of that cheerful Qi disappeared.

Every day when returning home, he developed the habit of bowing his head and gazing into the Pool of Shadows as he walked by, watching the bright reflections disappear one by one...

The Pool of Shadows will show you the silhouettes of the people you love. His master told him that once there was none left, he was ready to become the High Priest.

A High Priest cannot afford to have emotions.

That day finally came when his master, who had always preached the importance of not giving in to emotion, was so overcome with his obsessions that he transformed into an evil spirit.

Full of anguish, Qi banished his master's spirit with his spear. He was now destined to be Augran the High Priest, with no path back to his former self.

When Qi opened his eyes, his pupils had transformed, heaven and earth had changed, the pulse of the world was still, and his burning heart had run cold.

Tragedies without end had plagued this land. Now, he would be the one to end them. The Wilting, the broken Sky Dome, all would end when the Nine Seers patched up the sky.

He stepped out of the Marsh of Amnesia. The world lay roiling and clamoring before him.

Qi is dead. I am the Augran, High Priest of the Seers.

lore:
The Knights of the Round Table—known for their valor, honor, and virtue—have long guarded Eventide Cathedral. They hold a Martial Arts Tournament every autumn, an event that attracted crowds of spectators. Participants battle by day and make merry by night, in celebration of the annual harvest, and the ultimate victor of the tournament would be inducted into the Order.

Many brave Knights fell in battle over long years of war between the empire and the alliance. As their influence waned, they also succumbed to infighting and eventually split into factions. Their rivals hoped to exploit this weakness and plotted to exterminate the Knights in one fell swoop.

The annual Martial Arts Tournament was held as scheduled, and people flocked to Eventide Cathedral from all over the continent. The army of allied adversaries launched a surprise attack, sweeping through defenseless villages like a storm and departing quick as lightning, leaving burning ruins and weeping citizens in their wake.

This horrific tragedy was repeated three times in the span of only a few days. Eventide Cathedral fell into a state of panic, but the Knights of the Round Table were powerless to do anything about it. Without warning, the enemies launched an even fiercer attack on Eventide Cathedral itself. If they prevailed, the centuries-old glory of the Knights of the Round Table would be confined to history books forevermore.

The Knights made a hasty return, riding hard through the long night, but they were surprised at what they found upon arrival: Their sacred cathedral still towered high, while the blood and lopped-off heads they saw belonged to the despicable attackers. This feat was accomplished by a single man—a youth who had traveled from afar. In his hands was Excalibur, also known as the "Sword of Kings." According to legend, the sword had been fixed within a boulder by the Lady of the Lake, in dedication to the ancient and esteemed King Arthur.

The surviving citizens recounted the attack: The marauders had stormed the Cathedral as the crowd fled in all directions, and the young traveler's original sword broke in two during the clash. Seeing Excalibur protruding from the stone, he drew it out effortlessly and repelled the invaders.

The young man codenamed "Lam" was mercilessly exiled from his clan because they believed him to be an "inauspicious person" with the power of calamity hidden in his body. Lam's happiest days were those spent growing up with a group of orphans in a small fishing village next to the sea. When the flames of war extended there, Lam unexpectedly aroused the dormant "shark power" in his body and killed the vile enemy, protecting his friends.

The people were safe, but they were afraid of Lam's powers. Since then, the villagers regarded Lam as a monster, and no one dared to approach him. Whenever young Lam tried to use his powers to protect himself or others, he was met with frightened looks of rejection from everyone. Over time, Lam became accustomed to being away from the crowd and living alone.

In the war-torn Three Kingdoms, corpses lined the scorched battlefields. Lam's only means of survival was to rely on the fearsome power that made him an outcast to begin with. This orphan who survived the purgatory-like battlefields grew up and was adopted by Cao Cao, the Lord of Wei. There were many others like Lam in the Wei camp, whom Cao Cao had instructed should be taught the many combat arts, with the intention of developing a bevy of capable generals for his use.

In order to survive, Lam, who had finally found a place to live, was forced to shut his heart and numbly accept training. With his remarkable capabilities, Lam was naturally noticed by Cao Cao and given more tasks. All he could do to lessen the suffering of his opponents during missions was to wield his blade with swiftness and precision. Although he had long ceased to be that scared boy huddled up and trembling in a corner, and had gained calmness and courage—he had also lost all emotion.

lore:
Li Xin hails from Chang'an but has no place to call home. Chang'an was once his home. His father was originally the crown prince, but after being implicated in a treasonous plot, his entire family was persecuted. Bloodied and banished, Li Xin could only accept the dark power that his father had traded his life for.

While he was alone and despondent, Li Xin was confronted by an alchemist, who spoke confusing yet foreboding words, "You've lost Chang'an, and I've lost my most beloved possession. If you help me regain the Great Wall, I'll help you get back your city." Li Xin agreed to trade the Great Wall for Chang'an. Following the alchemist's instructions, he joined the alchemist's organization, the "Yaotian Society," and arrived at the borderlands with a burning desire for revenge. He would have to perform well there in order to eventually return to his true "home."

However, he detested the Great Wall. The isolation was maddening, but his pride and drive set him apart from his peers. A few veteran soldiers took no notice of his aloofness and approached him to chat. They told him that not long before, another man like him had volunteered to guard the Great Wall. He had been strong, but somehow suspicious. That man had escaped after murdering his commanding officer, and it was rumored that the traitor was still lingering nearby. Having finished the story, the veterans expected Li Xin to react with shock or fear. Instead, he simply inspected his sheathed blade and replied flatly, "Perfect. I'll give that traitor a taste of this."

Shortly after, a gang of thieves on horseback launched a surprise attack on the Great Wall. While the other soldiers were gearing up for battle, Li Xin stood alone, gazing in the direction of Dunefort with a curious expression on his face. He'd seen through the enemy's plotting. The thieves were only a diversion—their true target was Dunefort! Li Xin immediately reported this conclusion to the commander, who sent out a signal for reinforcements. Great Wall Guardians rode hard toward Dunefort. Li Xin searched the battlefield for the enemy's leader, seeking to snatch up top honors in combat achievement. After all, that aim was the only thing that made the isolation of the Great Wall endurable for him.

For thousands of years, the Great Wall was the fortress that defended the empire from outside threats. The Great Wall Guardians consisted of imperial soldiers, hastily armed pioneers, and people who simply couldn't find anywhere else to eke out a living.

Mulan was different. She was the first to volunteer to defend the wall.

Though a woman, she was just as valiant and hot-blooded as any man. With recognized prowess and supreme leadership skills, she fought alongside her people to repel the Feralis and bandits that coveted the wall.

Her excellent swordsmanship was a beautiful sight that left onlookers speechless, nullifying countless attacks from invading enemies.

But after one Ferali invasion in which the battle took a turn for the worse, rumors of a traitor spread through the guardians. They accused Mulan—the only one who had volunteered to guard the Great Wall—of being the traitor.

Despite the accusation and her tarnished reputation, she did not give up.

She began roaming the Wall, investigating Ferali activity and providing intelligence to the guardians. Although excluded by the other guardians, she still did her part to protect the Great Wall.

She traveled through the desert with her sword, keeping watch over the Great Wall and her homeland through a veil of sand. If the Great Wall Guardians needed her, she would be there to help them immediately.

lore:
"The Prince of Hadrian has returned!" they said. "Have you heard? After seven years without a word, the urchin prince has returned!" Their voices dripped with derision.

Hearing this proclamation upon emerging from the Outer City, Hakan tightened his hood. Urchin? The passersby didn't even try to hide the mockery in their words. But they had the situation right—Prince Hakan had been exiled soon after assuming the throne at a young age. He'd grown up amidst sandstorms and rolling dunes in a far-off land. The last time anyone in the capital had seen him was when Hakan was driven from power. There hadn't been much news of him since. It seemed like the whole outcast experience would haunt him forever.

"So why did he disappear?" a young girl inquired, pulling on the corner of her mother's clothes.

"I imagine he was just too ordinary to do anything of note. That's what happens to people who aren't brilliant enough. They're easily forgotten." The woman scoffed as she answered the girl's question.

"Then I'm gonna be brilliant! I don't want to be forgotten..." The girl nodded, scrunching up her face.

"How in the world did he get the throne in the first place?" the stall owner next to them interjected, unable to help himself.

"The former king had a lot riding on him. He thought the prince would be the one to take the Red Apple and fulfill the prophecy. I bet he sent the boy off to train because he discovered how little power he truly had," the woman replied, dropping a few bags of roasted chestnuts into her basket.

"I feel sorry for Grand Vizier! Serving the late king until his twilight years was no easy task, yet now the burden hasn't lessened at all with the useless new one... That'll be 40 lyras!" the stall owner gossiped as he tallied up the woman's bill.

lore:
A great river divides the Misty Marshes, with the city to the west and forest to the east.

Yaria is closely connected to this forest. Her parents once rescued an injured young deer which, despite their caring efforts, succumbed to its wounds shortly thereafter. The couple had not yet borne any children, but this was soon to change, and the husband and wife were convinced that their newborn daughter was somehow connected to that young deer; she was a human child, but also an embodiment of the deer's spirit.

A few years later, Yaria began studying under the scholar of the Misty Marshes, Guiguzi. Thanks to his guidance, she learned how to use magic to stimulate the growth of living things. With a simple swipe of her vine staff, she could summon vines, and trees to sprout from barren soil. Yaria was not yet adept at her newfound talent, however, and the life forms she created often turned into wisps of smoke soon after.

Yaria's power was growing stronger day by day, and so was her mischievous spirit. Not content with pulling pranks within her small corner of the forest, she dreamed of exploring the entire marshland. One day, she eventually wandered too far and came to a village outside the forest.

This village turned out to be the outskirts of the western city, situated upon land ruled by Eclipse. The villagers were terrified of Yaria, mistaking her for a monster. They tried to kill her and offer her as a sacrifice to Eclipse.

Yaria eventually made it back home at nightfall, covered in mud from head to toe. She recounted the greed and brutality of the villagers to her parents.

lore:
Ye, the capital city of the Wei kingdom, is a city of slaughter. The hustle and bustle of merchants is totally absent amidst its perennial yellow sands. Absent as well is the warbling song of birds. The only sound is that of armies marching among the rushing sands.

And yet Cai Yan loves this place. It's the place where she grew up, with all the people she cared about: her great foster father Cao Cao, the taciturn yet caring Dian Wei, along with those nameless soldiers with whom she loved to play. It is because of this love that Cai Yan wants to protect the place. Even as a young child, her mastery of the Hujia lute could always bring a smile to the citizens of Ye's faces with a cheery tune or two.

The lute was an heirloom gifted to her by her father, Cai Yong. As such, it also represented her deep affection for him. Her father was murdered when she was just a little girl, after which she was brought to Ye by Cao Cao, who claimed to be her father's dear friend, and raised as his foster daughter. Accompanying them on this journey to Ye was Dian Wei, her father's apprentice.

Dian Wei was an inarticulate man, but he was never at a loss for words when speaking of Cai Yong. Cai Yong had been his beloved teacher, a truly remarkable person and such a keen scholar that even Jixia Academy's knowledgeable sage Fuzi held him in high regard. Over the course of his lifetime, Cai Yong visited numerous sites to study ancient sorcery, and the Hujia lute was among the artifacts unearthed during his devoted research. Only regarding the circumstances of Cai Yong's death had Dian Wei never uttered a single word. Whenever the topic was brought up, he seemed to choke up and stumble over his words with a pained expression plastered on his face.

lore:
Sun Ce was born into a prestigious family in Jiang, but the extravagant lifestyle of the corrupt aristocracy never sat well with him.

He was forthright, passionate, and fearless. He lived amongst the common folk, empathizing with their sufferings and feeling disgusted with the injustices of the world. He yearned to tear down the parasitic world of the corrupt who fed upon the commoners and hoped to establish a fair and just kingdom in Wu—to let light penetrate the darkness so that all could prosper.

In order to cleanse Jiang of its corrupt aristocracy, Sun Ce joined forces with his best friend Zhou Yu. Together, they sailed Sun Ce's fleet of sturdy ships toward the battlefield.

According to Zhou Yu's plan, the day they sailed should have been a windy and the day they sailed should have been windy and beautiful. However, a tremendous thunderstorm soon appeared on the sea nearby, swirling strangely toward them as if it wanted to swallow up the fleet. Reading the wind and waves, Sun Ce deduced that this was no ordinary storm. Some powerful sorcerer was threatening Sun Ce and his crew, and they needed to evacuate the area quickly.

But he couldn't figure out which way to sail to shore.

Just then, a beam of light pierced the storm clouds. The beam seemed to be guiding them forward.

Without warning, the darkness suddenly evaporated, and the sea was bright once again.

Sun Ce glimpsed a beautiful maiden sitting on the shore, holding a lantern. He reached out his hand to show his gratitude.

The ships landed one by one, and by the day's end, Sun Ce's team had overwhelmed and defeated the aristocrats. Jiang had been returned to its true owners—the people. Sun Ce's dream had been fulfilled.

He and the maiden, too, became a couple to be envied.

lore:
Across the vast desert, Dun is known as the "Maverick Mercenary." It is said that whenever he throws his chain blade, known as the "Unruly Blade," he sneaks up on his target like a gust of wind and chops them down with his sword.

The legend of Dun's "hundred-person beheading" terrifies robbers and bandits alike. No one knows where he comes from, but everyone knows about his incredible strength. His reputation is second only to the legendary mercenary group "Dragon".

One evening, at an inn where mercenaries gathered, a suspicious man hiding under a black cloak piled a load of gold atop the bar, attracting the attention of everyone there.

"Go there and all this gold belongs to you." The man dressed in black spread out a map that had been scribbled all over and pointed to a place. The mercenaries chattered with excitement; This was a bounty they could only dream of!

"Unexplained business deals are always suspicious," Dun declared dubiously as he wiped down his blade.

"Afraid, are we?"

"No, but I'd be more tempted by a duel with you than your gold."

Dun's voice was drowned out by noise, as everyone gleefully took the gold and promised to meet at the given location.

Not long after, mercenaries, nomads, and those fleeing famine all poured out into the barren wasteland. Standing amidst dilapidated buildings, people talked about the upcoming mission, and whether they should pillage or get ready to be raided by nomads.

Unfortunately, what the mysterious man really wanted was their lives.

As Cao Cao was immersed in the satisfaction of his successful strategy, Dun staggered on wobbly legs, grasping his blade as if preparing to attack.

As he cast his spell from the sidelines, a look of shock crossed Sima Yi's face. He didn't expect anyone to be able to escape from his spell. He suddenly realized that Dun had paid the price of an eye in exchange for his life.

lore:
Sakeer was born in the secluded Firefly Valley. Like any other of his kin, he grew up beneath Firefly Ancestral Tree, where he listened to stories of the outside world. One day, when the stories his ancestors had left behind had all been told, there were no more stories to hear, and his tribe felt a great loss.

Inspired to venture out and bring back new stories, Sakeer packed up the ancestral storybook and the wooden sword his father had gifted him. He stealthily traversed the Stone Forest, which no one had ever crossed, and reached the "outside".

Sakeer was on cloud nine the first time he saw the vast lands of Alsahraa. He traveled across its various kingdoms and recorded several fascinating stories to bring back home. He made his way toward Madinat Erudit, where countless stories had been recorded, going all the way back to the birth of civilization.

But he accidentally entered the Madinat Fresco. By the time he came back out again, hundreds of years had somehow passed, and the once-prosperous oasis had turned to desert. Sakeer thought only of returning his home.

With the help of Garo and Prince of Lanling, Sakeer overcame many trials and tribulations. But when he finally made it back to his birthplace, he found that it had been lost to time. Firefly Valley, once so full of laughter and joy, had gone silent. Even the Firefly Ancestral Tree, the clan's eternal pride, had withered.

Sakeer was overcome with profound sadness, with tears running down his face. But instead of wallowing in sorrow, he followed his father's example and began telling his newly collected stories under the decaying Firefly Ancestral Tree.

lore:
An ancient creature born from the wishes of the Sandpura, this giant bird deity took a physical form to serve as their guardian. When he first appeared in the mortal realm, he granted people whatever they desired, heaping wealth and power on them. While his intent was to help them overcome the calamities facing them, in the end these blessings only bred greed and bloodshed. Realizing the complexity of human nature and drained from handing out countless blessings, the great bird exiled himself, vanishing into the clouds. Even though he still heard the people's prayers, visions of the bloody battles his blessings had enabled were fresh in his mind. Determined not to let his blessings breed disaster yet again, he used his long period of isolation to reflect on the cycles of cause and effect in the human world, until he was able to understand and embrace the nuances of humanity. Centuries later, a greedy lord plotted to awaken the great bird once more, intending to use its blessings to carry out his wicked scheme.

However, a papyrus letter drifted to Garuda Khageswara on the wind, bearing a cry for help from Sandpura Island once again. Garuda Khageswara had come to see that, aside from bestowing blessings, he also possessed the power to uphold justice. Golden-feathered arrows rained from the sky, striking down the greedy lord. In his dazzling radiance, treasures dissolved into golden light, streaking across the sky and into the horizon. From that moment on, the great bird became the "Wings of Judgment." Those who have too much will eventually lose their peace of mind. Those who have too little need but a few good seeds to start a new life. From then on, whenever people had more than they needed, they returned it to the great bird, balancing the scales. The great bird now presides over Azuria, upholding his philosophy of balance through judgment and preserving peace in the sea in the south.

lore:
The Great River divides the Misty Marshes, with a city to the west and a forest to the east.

Once a lone bird in the forest, Cirrus grew up in the company of a young deer, until one day, the flames of war consumed the Misty Marshes and the deer was killed by an arrow. Laden with sorrow, the lone bird decided to follow the deer into death and threw its body onto the rocks of a cliff.

As a witness to this, Misty Marshes' scholar, Guiguzi, sympathized with the lone bird's suffering and used the Spell of Reincarnation to give it new life and a new body. Though its body took on the form of a human, it could also fly and fight just like a bird.

He also received a new name—Cirrus.

However, the Art of Reincarnation did not fully erase memories of Cirrus's past life, and those memories caused excruciating pain whenever they resurfaced.

Later, wounded and blinded in a war, Cirrus fled to the city west of the Great River where he was taken in by the ruler, Eclipse, and became an emissary that managed the city for him.

Although Cirrus had lost his sight, he learned to envisage the world based on people's descriptions.

He would stretch out his wings and circle the city, tuning into the sounds and smells, sketching in his mind the lines as they should be, then drawing these lines on paper and giving them to his subordinates. The subordinates would then plot the residential and public areas in the city according to the lines, keeping the entire city neat and tidy.

According to Eclipse, the world from Cirrus's perspective was even clearer and more graceful than reality.
