lore:
Legend has it that many cities have risen throughout the history of Alsahraa, yet few ever manage to overcome the conflicts and chaos that ensue. Jade City is one of the exceptions, and it prospers due to the jade trade. Feyd, the eldest prince of Jade City, has become a household name in the city for a number of reasons: his profligate spending, heir to the throne, and the infamous lack of fixed employment as beneficiary of the public purse. Being a king or a hero is never his desire. The only certain facts are Feyd's dedication to staying rich and idle, and his love for jade. Beautiful jade is a common pursuit among the people of Jade City, and as one known as the Jaded Son from birth and the possessor of the ability to control Soul Jade, Feyd is no exception. He never gets tired of sending his jade craftsmen out searching and carving jade into various masterpieces for his collection, or to be given away as gifts.

According to the people of Jade City, he is a dashing young man with no regard for money; but to the officials, he is a free-spirited prince who does as he pleases. Yet his younger brother Saeed finds it impossible to believe that the outstanding older brother he grew up with has been reduced to such an idle critter. Love and hate toward Feyd coexist in Saeed's heart.

Yet no one knows that at the age of 14, Feyd, whose sole wish was to continue his extravagant and carefree princely life, witnessed his father's miserable death at the hands of General Roya. Once Roya took control of the city, as the older brother, Feyd could do nothing more than hide his hatred deep within while playing the role of the useless prince. Nor would anyone know that it was the only reason Feyd could avoid Roya's cunning gaze, move in the shadows, and help the senior officials escape death right under Roya's nose. Feyd even managed to secretly plan out and execute the rescue of his younger brother Saeed, who'd been held at the Great Wall since the incident in the market. After years of planning and subterfuge, when his younger brother's plans were discovered by Roya during an evilly planned feast, Feyd just went ahead and took vengeance with his own hands. It was Garo and the others who helped him escape danger after getting severely injured during the ordeal. Yet, during Saeed’s long-desired Hero's Eve, in order to protect his younger brother and Jade City, Feyd was forced to once again put an end to the schemes in a way Saeed couldn't accept. Over the years, he's been hiding many a truth deep within. Happy-go-lucky and frivolous on the outside, yet secretly protecting everything he loves while endlessly searching for the secrets lurking beneath Jade City's bustling appearance.

lore:
The Feralis are a species that existed on the continent before humans.

The arrival of the superbeings heralded the beginning of solar energy. Yearning for it, the feralis made a pact with the superbeings that allowed the Feralis to maintain the Sun Tower for the superbeings. But in the eyes of the superbeings, the feralis were nothing but uncivilized, beast-like creatures, and they made them toil endlessly without ever fulfilling their promise.

This was a dark and cruel time for the Feralis.

Wukong is a Ferali, but he was stubborn, and untamed. While being oppressed, he realized the Feralis were being taken advantage of, and he launched a rebellion, leading the Feralis in a bid for freedom.

Wukong swept across the continent like a golden hurricane. Wherever he went, he struck fear into the hearts of humans and rulers while slaves cheered and shouted slogans of freedom.

The anxious rulers summoned a powerful Aorian in an attempt to subdue Wukong. However, Wukong just laughed and waved his weapon, and where his Golden Cudgel struck, the shackles of oppression shattered, freeing the Aorians. Those who were freed shouted Wukong's name and joined the ranks of the rebellion.

Over time, more and more slaves joined Wukong's cause. His ranks grew so large that the humans thought that the continental regime would be overturned.

This was the first Ferali rebellion in the history of the continent. However, the Ferali force was later betrayed and the rebellion ended in failure.

lore:
In a village by the river dwelled Ukyo Tachibana, the descendant of a fallen samurai family. He was known for his mastery over Iaijutsu, the quickdraw sword technique. His soft demeanor captivated the hearts of young women, none of whom suspected that he was in fact very lonely and felt empty inside. This was because he had suffered from a respiratory disease for many years, and he was convinced that he would die alone.

One day, everything changed. To flee the pestilence of the city, a Lord took his family to the countryside, and Ukyo Tachibana encountered Kei Odagiri, the equally quiet daughter of the Lord. Her soft words and dignified aura stood out, but due to the differences in their social standings, they rarely saw each other.

Kei was trying to pick the blooming flowers on the cliff for her ill mother when their paths crossed. Ukyo picked them for her, and Kei expressed her gratitude. "Do you like flowers, too? I was moved by their beauty." Like tossing a stone into a quiet lake, her words sent ripples through Ukyo Tachibana's heart, and he wanted to live more than ever, so he could pick all the flowers for the girl that he loved.

The pestilence was still spreading, and the villagers lived in fear. Kei was worried because her mother was still sick, when news came that the flowers blooming in the capital could cure any sickness and extend life. Looking at his frustrated lover, Ukyo Tachibana decided to go to the capital, which, in addition to the plague, was also threatened by the zealous Blood Clan. But if the flowers there could bring her smile back...

With Nameless, his hand-forged blade, Ukyo Tachibana left for the capital.

lore:
Since time immemorial, mercenaries have bounced between different masters, using their blood and sweat to earn themselves a living. Crisis, danger, betrayal, and death were all in a day's work for them. Today's friends might become tomorrow's enemies, and adversaries of the past might become allies of the present.

And yet one stood out from the crowd. The man known as "Zilong" wasn't your average hired hitman. With his charismatic leadership, he united and nurtured a ragtag bunch of outlaws into a powerful mercenary group named "Dragon". Cao Cao had contracted Zilong's services several times, and seeing his mercenary organization grow stronger and stronger, Cao Cao decided he'd like them to belong to him permanently. Needless to say, Zilong refused.

This event kicked off an intricate plot. Thereafter, Cao Cao began to stoke the flame of Zilong's ambition. Zilong eventually desired to abandon his status as a mere mercenary and instead become the one standing above the rest. Killing the warlord Lu Bu would be the first step toward achieving this dream.

But someone in the organization opposed the idea. Known as "Shadow", he had long been Zilong's closest friend and right-hand man. Unbeknownst even to Cao Cao, "Dragon" was in fact a cooperation between these two men: the organization's namesake was responsible for their clientele and assignments, but Shadow was the real, raw force behind the organization.

This was the first time the pair had ever had a serious disagreement. Shadow opposed Zilong's ambition and did not believe that Cao Cao would fully support anyone who might eventually become a threat to himself. Zilong, however, felt that he had everything under control. To Shadow, it was a massive gamble—one that put the lives of all the group's members at stake. Unable to persuade Zilong, Shadow left the organization.

lore:
Born into an illustrious family in Chang'an, Ying had always dreamed of becoming a hero.

As a child, she used to climb the walls of the local teahouse to listen to the storyteller recount tales of Lady Li, who had set out on horseback to guard the borderlands, and who—despite being a woman—eventually became a great general. Wielding her blazing spear, she could repel hundreds of enemy troops all by herself.

Ying longed to emulate such a heroine, so she began carrying around a wooden spear that was even longer than she was tall. She did her best to imitate Lady Li, chanting the spear mantra she half understood and practicing every day, rain or shine.

Accompanied by her spear, Ying grew up day by day, but people viewed her as being negligent of her duties as a young noblewoman. Still inspired by Lady Li's fearsome flaming spear, Ying tried to figure out how to set her spear alight. Having tried and failed with both cotton and charcoal, Ying finally got her hands on a chunk of saltpeter, which she fastened to the end of her spear and swung around on the city's streets. When the spear-tip brushed against something, sparks would fly.

"My spear is on fire, just like Lady Li's!"

Ying's sharp shout startled the pigeons resting nearby...

One day, those sparks accidentally kindled a furious blaze outside the city. After the flames were finally extinguished, her father snatched up her spear and snapped it in two. "You don't even know what it means to wield a spear!"

lore:
To the south of [Primaera] lies a string of pearl-like isles, known as Azuria.

In Azuria, the lakes are not cradled by the land. Rather, there are "lakes" of land surrounded by endless ocean. The sons and daughters of the ocean share the same blue sky and open waters with the mysterious beasts born in this land. Even Azuria's oldest inhabitants cannot say whence the leviathans came, only that they hold a strange power to calm the fury of nature. For countless years, they have roamed these far-off seas, sometimes as silent watchers, sometimes as steadfast guardians of humanity.

Nectam is home to one such beast, the great sea serpent Bakunawa. With a temperament shaped by ocean gales, jagged reefs, and briny shores, it kept its distance from humankind, claiming Nectam's nutgall tree forest as its domain. The people of Nectam both feared and revered it, and legend told of a human who once earned its blessing, only to be petrified and become part of the reefs. Sometimes, when the moon is full, it would leap out of ocean, as though it would swallow the moon itself. Children would make up songs about the "moon-eater" that rode upon the sea breeze and dwelled in the nutgall forest.

All in all, Nectam is one of the string of pearly isles that make Azuria.

Lapulapu, the datu, or chief, of Nectam, often gazed off at the horizon where azure sky and cerulean water met, lost in the tranquility of the island. The sea breeze carried the chants of fishermen, their faith anchored in a future where they could earn with their own hands. Decisive and forceful—that is Lapulapu. Yet in his youth, he was spirited, open-hearted, and quick to trust, joining the children's songs about the great sea serpent and watching eagerly for the rock turtles' return. Such innocence, however, cannot win a chieftain's seat. His new standing rests on his might, his stratagems, and his ability to inspire. The darker turns of politics aside, he is still a datu his people could depend on, the defender of the isles and their nutgall tree forest.

But one fateful day, that all changed.

It was the day the rock turtles were supposed to return.

Only this time, as the islanders looked out to sea, they saw not rock turtles but a fleet of invaders. The fleet was led by a datu from a neighboring island, seeking to gain control of Nectam's nutgall trees and surrounding sea. They never had the blessing of any mighty beasts, nor had they ever made waves. But now, they were flying bright flags and bore new, razor-sharp weapons and shields emblazoned with a helix pattern. Lapulapu did not have the time to ponder why this petty faction had suddenly decided to invade. He saw that war was inevitable, and the one thought that dominated his mind was that Nectam could not be taken. Assessing the situation, he noted that although the enemy did not look like the strongest fighters, they have the advantage of well-crafted weaponry. Nectam might have a fighting chance, if they are willing to make some sacrifices.

lore:
Musashi grew up obsessed with the blade. From a young age, he aspired to reach the pinnacle of swordsmanship and become the world's greatest samurai. This aspiration was hindered, however, by his family's poverty. They could not afford to pay for training, so he was mercilessly kicked out of the dojo every time he managed to find a way to sneak in. The kind-hearted owner of the sweets shop across the street from the dojo took pity on Musashi, and he made a deal with the dojo master to let his tuition be paid in sweets daily.

Whenever her daughter, Otsu, brought the sweets to the dojo, she always saw Musashi getting knocked to the ground by a student much taller than him. But as soon as he saw her, he would leap up from the ground and wave at her as if nothing had happened. As the days went by, the two became childhood sweethearts.

One night, drunken hooligans started causing trouble at the sweets shop. Musashi appeared out of nowhere, charging forward to protect Otsu with his wooden training swords. He managed to drive the hooligans away but was injured in the process. As Otsu tended his wounds, feeling guilty for having caused them, Musashi made a solemn promise. "Do not be afraid. I will become the world's greatest samurai, and I will protect you."

Musashi took his oath to heart, training arduously and even developing his own Niten Ichiryuu technique. He roamed Kyokutou, challenging every samurai he came across. Never losing a duel, his reputation quickly grew.

One day, as Musashi was leaving home, Otsu handed him an amulet. She smiled and said, "Before every duel, you must first declare your name. That way, no matter where I am, I'll hear news of you."

Legends began to circulate in Kyokutou about a dual-bladed samurai. His technique was exquisite, and he introduced himself before every duel. "My name is Musashi, and I am the one who shall defeat you." No one in Kyokutou could match his skills, putting him one step closer to the pinnacle to which he'd always aspired.

Kaizer was born into an ancient clan of Anomalics in Navenia. His lineage possessed truly extraordinary power. But Kaizer eventually traced the source of the power and discovered a shocking truth: His family's power was ill-begotten, and the lineage thus carried a terrible curse.

Having gained their power through evil, the family would eventually have to pay the price. Kaizer decided to shoulder this burden himself, heading out in search of a way to end the curse. He abandoned his homeland, leaving behind only fearsome legends...

Year upon year, the demon blade wandered the continent like a ghost, striking fear into the hearts of his fellow Anomalics. Kaizer struck out toward the east, pursuing the very roots of sorcery in the scant hope of freeing himself from his tormented fate.

And that is how he came upon the deserts of Alsahraa. Dunefort, the capital of the prosperous empire and an oasis amidst the desert, should have been brimming with vitality. But all Kaizer found was destruction. The imperial court had fallen, and with it, Dunefort had collapsed as well.

Dunefort's fate held no interest for Kaizer, but the overflowing of sorcery there disgusted him. It reminded him of the nightmare that tormented him day and night. While citizens fled at the sight of him, Kaizer strode into the heart of the disaster. Suddenly, he realized that behind this carnage must lie a skilled sorcerer, one who was still admiring the results of their evildoing.

Lacking not confidence nor pride, Kaizer vowed to find that person. Unwilling to face Kaizer's power head-on, the hidden sorcerer tried to use illusions to ensnare him in suffering and despair. Kaizer saw through the illusions. Empowered by his forceful will, a swipe of Kaizer's blade sliced through the evil mist like a fierce gale.

lore:
Madness devoured his body.

This is not the age of man. To survive, one must become a beast.

The imposing Dian Wei is kneeling in a military tent. His future overlord, Cao Cao, stands before him, evaluating how loyal he will be, and how valuable that loyalty may prove.

"Frenzy. A unique mutation that appears in those with the Ferali gene." Donning a black robe, Sima Yi calmly explains what makes Dian Wei so special. The Feralis are the continent's aboriginals. They look like beasts, and they have suffered long-standing mistreatment at the hands of humans. However, those with Ferali blood possess exceptional power.

As Sima Yi explains it, "The frenzy vastly increases the mental and physical strength of the one affected, not to mention their combat abilities. The downside is that the ability to reason is lost. Though rationality returns once the frenzy fades, it never fully recovers."

"All I need is a loyal servant. A useful servant... No. A loyal pet," Cao Cao proclaims.

Dian Wei trembles. Even in a world as chaotic as this, beasts, with their inability to feel pain, will find a way to survive. But the young, delicate infant besides him, Little Lute, is a different story altogether. Dian Wei will never forget that he was the one who caused the death of Little Lute's father, his teacher who had given him so much.

Dian Wei had been despised and abandoned by humans for quite some time before meeting his teacher. Cai Yong's mercy and patience shone into Dian Wei's dark heart like a heavenly light, turning him from a beast into a man. With Cai Yong's encouragement, Dian Wei even managed to save a whole city by himself, thereby marking his first military accomplishment. At that time, Dian Wei was sure that he could live a life of reason like a normal person... or even attain glory in the name of righteousness like a heroic warrior.

However, this hope was crushed by a bout of madness, and Dian Wei once again slipped into a dark abyss.

The Cai family had been slaughtered. The only survivor was Cai Yong's daughter, Little Lute. Seeing this innocent infant in his arms, smiling without a worry in the world, shatters Dian Wei's heart.

Even if awakening meant that the lives of those he loved would be lost, it would still be better than descending further into madness, where infinite doom is the only certainty. He makes a simple decision: Carry out Cao Cao's orders to ensure that Cai Yong's daughter can grow up in safety...

lore:
Primaera is home to the ancient Anomalic clans, who inherit the blood of the Feralis of bygone ages. They can obtain magical powers more easily than common humans, but this ability comes with a cruel price. Luna was born into just such a clan, and she was raised to be its heir.

Her clan's specialty was the power to imbue weapons with the power of nature. At Luna's coming-of-age ceremony, she chose to take the power of the Lunar Goddess as her own. Thus, she has since been known as Lady Moonblade. By law, only one clan member could inherit its power. Luna's seven brothers and sisters, though not chosen, should have been able to go on with their lives as common people. But on one full moon night, tragedy struck.

Moonlight shone coldly on the ground as her eldest brother, her most beloved family, murdered her parents, relatives, and all of her other siblings.

"You're no match for me, little sister," the man with the disfigured face growled.

"What have you done?! If you wanted to be the heir, I would have let you! Why have you gone and killed our entire family?!"

"Don't you remember, sister? You were ten years old. Killers burst into our village and took you hostage. I slaughtered them all."

"I... Yes, I remember..."

"I didn't even do it to save you. I just couldn't control myself."

The Anomalics possessed great power, but that very power could also drive them mad. Luna realized that this was what had happened to her brother.

lore:
There once was a man who rode a fish and loved to dream, and his name was Zhuangzi.

In the world of dreams, nothing held Zhuangzi back. Sometimes he dreamed that he had turned into a butterfly—or that it was a butterfly who had turned into him. The butterfly fluttered its wings, triggering a reverberation that kicked up a storm upon the continent.

Sometimes he dreamed that he merged completely with the will of nature, no longer being bound by the rules of reality, his awareness becoming one with the heavens.

For as long as he could remember, everything Zhuangzi dreamed would eventually come to pass in reality—a rather uncommon and fantastic ability. One day, Zhuangzi dreamed that he transformed into a butterfly that glowed with a strange light. In waking life, naturally, people were frightened of him and dared not approach.

Then one day, Zhuangzi conjured up a vast otherworld but could find no place to put it. Zhuangzi finally realized that he no longer belonged in his hometown, so he set out from his home in search of a place where he could truly be accepted.

A sovereign got word of Zhuangzi's ability to transform dreams into reality and asked to hire his services. Though the reward was generous, Zhuangzi declined the invitation. He had no desire for his dreams to become some tribute intricately carved on an altar, nor a tool employed to fulfill a thirst for power, and even less so did Zhuangzi want to turn his fantastic ability into just a way to get rich. He only wanted to dream whatever he pleased, unfettered by the rules of the mortal world.

Eventually, Zhuangzi arrived at a place known as Jixia. There, he wandered the mountains and forests, admired the stars by night, and was finally able to dream his dreams to the fullest.

lore:
Lu Bu managed to get away from the enemies that had surrounded him, but his injuries were too serious, and he fell on the side of the road, gasping for breath. His wounds attracted flies, but the odious insects never got to devour their enormous prey. A wandering caravan stopped, and gentle hands delivered water to his lips. Her hands were soft. "Live." Her voice was a whisper from heaven. That one word triggered his survival instinct. He fought death, and wrested his life from its grasp.

Night fell. The grass swayed in the wind as the girl danced by the fire. The man teetering on the edge of death was spellbound. Was he dreaming? Dreams, fleeting dreams. How many years had passed since then? He had superhuman strength, and was undefeated. But when people talked about the Warlord, they spoke of his recklessness and lack of strategy. Lu Bu scoffed quietly to himself. They either wanted to use him, or they wanted him dead. A cruel world indeed. Some may be willing to become a weapon for others, like... Bai Qi. But Lu Bu was not interested in such a fate. "I will stay alive, and obtain everything I want." He had endured it all silently through betrayal after betrayal. Just a little more... He had thought he would have it all.

Until the woman named Diaochan danced before him. He had seen a dream in her movements—a long time ago, by a bonfire far away. That flash of joy had been beautiful, like the spring of life... a memory he'd revisited over and over. And he woke up, once again. His body fell, but his mind was clear. He opened up his heart to her, but it ended in his tragic downfall. It was the end for the hero.

Xu Fu laughed raspily. "You have a choice, you know?" What choice? Live on, and be punished through reincarnation? Live because no one wants to die, though everyone wanted you dead. "There's a great secret of this world hidden in the Heavenly Scrolls," said Xu Fu. "I've been trying to uncover it, and you're my best bet." "If you don't want to give in to reincarnation, then surpass it."

Navenian society is divided into three levels, and its people also have their strict places in society.

At the highest level are the ruling aristocracy. Generation after generation of the nobility have maintained the order and prosperity of Navenia. The middle level is comprised of merchants. The merchants' trade provides substantial funding for Navenia's research into machinery.

These merchants also reap the benefits that machinery provides. At the lowest level of Navenia are those like Biron—the poor.

Biron was a well-known mercenary in Navenia. Whenever his name came up in conversation, people would say, "Oh, that's the fool who challenged the Mecha Commander."

When he was very young, Biron scraped together a living through hard labor at the docks. There, he encountered a man named Mr. Polo, who was traveling to the East in search of a way to get access to the curse. Despite the fact that Biron would not see this kind soul again, or even be able to clearly recall his face, Polo's drive to act in pursuit of his ideals left a lasting impression on Biron.

After he came of age, Biron became a guard, accompanying groups of merchants all over Sunset. He gradually began to observe changes in Navenia—polluted water, corrosion, and crystallization.

These changes struck fear into his heart. And so, he began to search for the cause of the pollution.

One morning, this search led the lowly mercenary before Milady, the "Mecha Commander" herself. He presented her with a glimmering piece of crystal.

lore:
Chang'an was the most prosperous city in the empire. A legend surrounding this city had long spread amongst scholars of the continent that Chang'an had been built upon a stone foundation that had existed since ancient times. This stone slab was the source of power for all the machinery of the city and was known as the "Heart of Chang'an."

The city "gate," an unobtrusive standing archway, dusty and covered in cobwebs, sat right atop the foundation stone. People passed the gate day after day, totally unaware of the protector who surveyed their every step. This surveillance had been constant for a long, long time.

That protector was Kui.

Since long ago—long before Chang'an even existed—Kui had stood within the archway and guarded it in silence. Humans built walls atop the great foundation stone, then divided the area into settlements and marketplaces, and eventually built an entire city, naming it "Chang'an." Thereafter, Chang'an grew prosperous, bringing together people from all around the world. Some of them had come to place sorcerous seals, some to transport dangerous machinery, and some had come with plots and schemes... But none of them escaped Kui's keen eyes and ears.

Yet Kui never meddled in mundane affairs and never intervened in any strife between humans. His only duty was to guard the foundation stone and the city built upon it. The city's power was tied directly to the Heart of Chang'an, and anyone within the city limits was powerless to resist such a force. As long as the stone was safe, Chang'an was safe.

When people passed the archway during the day, Kui would not appear before them. Only at midnight would the "gate" open, and Kui would step out onto Phoenix Avenue to begin his patrol of the city.

In the inky darkness of night, Kui's massive frame paced soundlessly through the streets and alleys of Chang'an. Upon discovering anyone who sought to harm Chang'an or those who coveted the mysterious power of its foundation stone, Kui would swallow them into a chaotic void that penetrated to the ancient past, burying them in eternal darkness, to be accompanied only by their shameful desires.

After she reached adulthood, she kept dreaming about following in the silhouette of a man and calling his name over and over.

"I must really love this man," she thought.

Her family records contained details of a brutal conflict surrounding the Secret Tome, which was supposedly destroyed, but there were rumors of unauthorized copies, stained by blood, being passed around.

An ancestor that was involved in the conflict was also named Mai. Was this a coincidence, or...? The Mai from the history fell in love with the adopted son of the martial artist who possessed the Secret Tome. The silhouette of this man from another land, only described in words at first, eventually became the figure in Mai's dreams.

When Xu Fu sailed across the sea to Kyokutou to boast about the effects of the immortality pills, the nobles were charmed by his words. At some point, even the half-ferali disciples of the Shiranui School were captivated, and started working for Xu Fu. Hanzo tried to stop them, but his opposition fell on deaf years, and Xu Fu saw Hanzo as an obstacle.

And then news from the capital told of a ship that arrived from the west. Its foreign crew, with blue eyes and blonde hair, was under siege by the agitated Blood Clan. Mai was anxious... Was the man in her dreams one of them? She went to see her grandfather and requested to go to the capital.

Mai Shiranui left for the capital to search for the man in her dreams. But shortly after her departure, a messenger caught up with her and told her that Hanzo had been brutally slain by a traitor. Mai Shiranui realized that, like the Mai from her family records, she was now involved in the conflict over the Secret Tome and foreigners from another land.

But misfortune struck the family one day. Ships that received orders to sail eastward kept sinking around the Tonpuu Shore, and these incidents triggered unrest in the city, as the families of the missing crew begged for explanations, and merchants that suffered huge losses banded together to demand compensation. Many knights, who came to serve the family because they admired the family's reputation, chose to depart.

The pirates also assembled and launched an attack on the family, who failed to defend themselves. The pirates took over the villas, and the remaining family members decided to pay a ransom to salvage what little glory they have left.

Only Charlotte refused, because to a noble, losing honor was worse than death.

Before they reached an agreement with the pirates, she paid a visit to the pirate ship with her sword. After a full night of fighting, she defeated every single pirate and exiled them from the city.

But things didn't end there. No one knew why the ships sank, and the source of the unrest has not been identified. She needed to bring closure to the grieving families and the dead sailors.

After sorting through the leads she had, she thought the answers she was looking for might be in Kyokutou, a city to the east. With her sword and red roses by her side, and her duty to protect the family reputation on her shoulder, she boarded a ship that took her to faraway places, just like her ancestors did.

The ancient city of Yi used to be one of the most prosperous cities when it came to machinery. Under Liu Bei's instruction, Kongming drafted a series of measures that made the city a great hub for scholars, with a thriving research scene. New machinery inventions are still produced here to this very day.

It's hard being a genius, but it's even harder when your mentor is also a genius. From birth, the biggest worry in the life of Liu Shan, the young lord of the Shu kingdom, was how to prove himself not only as the successor of his father, Liu Bei, and his mentor, Kongming, but also better than both of them.

When he was seven, Liu Shan crashed his infamous wooden ox cart into three houses and one pigsty, which proved that making deadly vehicular weapons was possible. From then on, Liu Shan's reputation as a genius began to spread in Yi.

When he was eight, he made his debut on the battlefield. As a backup driver, he dumped bales of grain in the river during the dry season, creating a shortcut for the troops and making an unexpected contribution to their final victory.

When he was ten, he was no longer satisfied with just being a driver, so he started designing a brand-new destructive vehicle. It was both powerful and eye-catching, with its panda-shaped design. It even had a special seat that adjusted to the driver's height. The vehicle was the talk of the town for a time. And obviously, the houses, farmland, and forests destroyed in Liu Shan's many test runs were all compensated for by his father Liu Bei and his mentor Kongming.

By the time he was twelve years old, he had extensively upgraded his vehicle and named it "M-1". He was ready to give it a thorough testing, so the little genius made the most important decision of his life: to run away from home!

Ever vibrant and free-spirited, she was like a little sun, always bringing light and warmth to those around her. During her studies at the Seerglade Academy, her name was tied to countless stories: skipping classes, causing trouble, venturing into forbidden forests, challenging authority, getting punished with her partners in crime... She bonded with everyone in her year, and even became soul buddies with Donghuang and the late Augran.

However, Lumina's life ended tragically in that disaster twenty years ago. Tales recounted that she fought valiantly as Austren until her final breath. With her fall, the Bird Tribe who served as sentinels perished from history, and became a mere legend of Misty Marshes.

But stories are just that—stories. The witnesses to these events have long since passed, leaving no way to verify the truth. For the storytellers, it's just another "heroic stand in the forest" story. But now the power of life has bloomed again, and the girl who has slumbered in the underworld for twenty years has awaken.

She has returned to the Misty Marshes, but no longer as Austren. Umbrosa's path of destruction has officially begun.

lore:
Lian Po was born in the Gandan clan of the Southlands, a poor and unstable region. The clan owned a mine that put their wealth significantly above the other clans in the area, but they were not very powerful, so they were often pillaged by the poorer clans nearby.

Eventually, Lian Po became a general of the clan, and their military prowess grew. The clans nearby found themselves unable to rob Gandan anymore, and his success on the battlefield led to the clan electing him their leader.

The other clans were afraid of Lian Po and the Gandan clan, and stopped attacking them. However, this also meant that they had lost their livelihood. Lian Po did not want to see his neighbors plagued by hunger and poverty, so he decided to send aid, and even opened up a portion of the mines to them. The clans eventually merged, and Gandan enjoyed peace for a long time.

But the peace did not last. Xu Fu, and the Blood Clan that he created through sorcery, started a war. When a city asked for help, Lian Po, who was already in his fifties, led his elite soldiers to the city without hesitation.

When they reached the city, Lian Po was stopped by a young man with a scythe in his hand. "I'll deal with the Blood Clan here. Don't go any further."

He was Bai Qi, also known as the ultimate weapon.

Having lived in Gandan his whole life, Lian Po had not heard of Bai Qi. Even if he had, he did not tolerate being underestimated, for Bai Qi had ignored them and walked into the city alone.

Lian Po ordered his people to set up camp by the gate, and waited.

Throughout the night, wailing echoed through the city. When the first light of the day lit the dark, the wailing stopped, and a bloodied Bai Qi appeared at the gate. He had slaughtered every single Blood Clan member by himself, and saved the city.

Bai Qi's feat shook Lian Po to his core, and his fighting spirit was afire. To protect his people and prove his worth, he traveled to the Jixia Academy to seek new strength.

lore:
Zhang Fei was born to a family of Human-Ferali hybrids. The family hid their secret for many years, living normal lives as machinists in human settlements.

But five years ago, their friends and neighbors learned of their Ferali blood. A crazed mob wielding stones and farm tools chased them into the center of town. This was the age of humans, and there was no room to coexist with feralis or their ilk.

Their workshop was up in flames behind them as their loved ones fell one after another before them. The blood in their bodies began to boil as their chains rattled and their limbs transformed. Muscles straining against their clothing, their self-restraint finally shattered. Howling like beasts with blood-red eyes, they prepared to devour the crowd.

Suddenly, the crowd parted to reveal Senior Officer Du You of the city of Yi.

The machinist thought frantically, "By the light of day, he had nothing but praise for my machines. Has he now come to execute me?"

But Du You calmed the crowd and brought the dying craftsman to his home. The next five years sped by.

The machinist hid away in his benefactor's mansion, plying his craft in exchange for a safe place to stay. He toiled night and day throughout his self-imprisonment. Only while tinkering and tuning, it seemed, could he suppress the rage that threatened to consume him—and everything around him.

One day, Zhang Fei was tinkering with a strange, ancient-looking iron box that Du You had handed him. The box would not open, but the work was another welcome distraction from the dark thoughts that plagued him. That is, until the box emitted a short, crisp sound and suddenly a wave of understanding washed over him...

lore:
Nakoruru is a witch who has the ability to communicate with all living creatures. An eagle named Mamahaha fights by her side. As a witch with an affinity for nature, she can hear the voices of everything. But the wind only carried bad news: bloody creatures from the other side of the ocean arriving, and the soul of the nature wailing in pain.

An escapee named Xu Fu quietly arrived at Kyokutou. The immortality pill that he offered mesmerized the nobles, who became part of the Blood Clan. The pestilence of blood started to spread like wildfire. To make matters worse, many volunteered to become a Blood Clan member in exchange for eternal life. Then they started killing each other for food.

Mamahaha flapped its wings anxiously as the smell of blood permeated the village. Nakoruru kept having the same dream, in which Kyokutou sunk into a sea of blood. If this went on, Kyokutou, as well as the spirit of nature, would die. The worried Nakoruru decided to take Mamahaha and travel to the capital.

It was worse than she imagined. The pedestrians looked like ordinary humans, but their eyes hungered for blood. In the end, they reached a dilapidated village where everyone died in the Blood Clan uprising, and the land was scarred. Mamahaha circled above the village, and its calls guided Nakoruru to hear the voice of a girl, who told a story about how she lost her childhood friend in the Blood Clan uprising, and of promises that could no longer be kept. The boy who was looking to become the best in the world was no more.

When the morning light arrived, Nakoruru and Mamahaha prayed for the girl in the name of the spirit of nature and resumed their journey. The brutal Blood Clan, the wailing nature, and the people who lost their loved ones...

Nakoruru would never let any of that happen again.

lore:
The young Yang Jian had a secret, a secret that nobody knew about. A "third eye" was hidden within his forehead. Though the eye couldn't be seen from the outside, the power it contained could always be felt. No one could tell him what it was, but he was certain that he was different from regular humans, which made him very careful to stay away from others. People envied the boy’s good luck, commented on his indifference and arrogance, and praised his elegance and strength behind his back. But in the warm sunset, he looked at the carefree human children with envy and watched as the hot-tempered and stubborn Nezha got into fights with others. During this time, only the stray puppies he picked up became his companions.

Like many of those born to nobility, he was sent to Celestia to study sorcery when he was very young. He stood out as a rare genius and was finally chosen by Nuwa to be her successor.

"You are my heir. One day, this world will be handed over to you to protect." The majestic mentor Nuwa pointed to an incredibly exquisite mechanism and said to the young boy, "You will be the incarnation of the will to protect this world." The mechanism before him was the core of a superbeing object called the "Ark." The soil beneath where it had landed was named the Original Lands.

"You must work harder than me to protect this world! If you don't... you will allow tragedy to happen again..."

The harsh words echoed in the boy's heart for a long time. The power in his "third eye" surged.

Outside of the glorious Original Lands, the Feralis rebelled from time to time. The boy gradually grew into a young man and was ordered to patrol the land to hunt Feralis. His ingenuity and sorcery were unmatched. Though hunting hardened his heart, the invisible eye on his forehead constantly reminded him of the question: "Who am I?"

The legend of the Dark Master has been known throughout the continent for years and years. He represented absolute darkness, and it was prophesied that he would pull the world into an abyss of destruction. Although his body had been destroyed, his spirit still roamed the mortal realm, and he could be reborn with a new identity at any moment.

Jiang Ziya, the Sanctifier, and his disciples vigilantly monitored all anomalous activity on the continent, searching for the dark master's reincarnation. After hundreds of years, they finally found some traces in the Riverlands, and Jiang Ziya foretold that the next Dark Master would appear there.

At the same time, a new host of heroes emerged from the Riverlands, seeking to resist the brutal rule of the Omniscients. Xiang Yu was one of the strongest warriors among them, and he gathered a group of allies to form his own army. Through battles large and small, his sphere of influence expanded rapidly until finally, he had a chance at becoming the next king of the Riverlands.

Some were jealous of his military achievements, others feared his power, while others tried to set traps for him to fall into... In any case, more and more people heard of Jiang Ziya's prophecy, and they began to suspect that Xiang Yu was the Dark Master. People began to despise him, and even attempted to finish him off before the power of the Dark Master was fully awakened.

But Xiang Yu did not believe in fate, and moreover, he did not appreciate being cast away by the world. While facing hostility from all corners, Xiang Yu encountered Consort Yu. She was the only one who trusted him. They fought alongside one another, and over time, a deep love blossomed between them.

As the war advanced, the Omniscients were overthrown, leaving Xiang Yu with only one worthy adversary, Liu Bang. The two would have to fight to determine who would be the new king.

At the time the duel was set to begin, Liu Bang ambushed Xiang Yu, who was quickly surrounded by thousands upon thousands of enemies, while Consort Yu had vanished without a trace. As the furious night wind wailed, countless torches burned bright as day, and scores of war-horses whinnied anxiously on the battlefield. Such an enormous force had been summoned, all to put a single man to death.

When she got older, she wandered the land and eventually reached Jixia, then enrolled as a student at Jixia Academy. Eccentric, aloof, and arrogant, even Fuzi had a hard time communicating with her.

She firmly believed that both power and gold were required for survival, so she occasionally joined the troops in Yong to earn her mercenary's purse.

Repulsed by the shackling of the Ferali troops, she shattered the chains with her hammer. The sovereign of Yong, Zheng, and his generals had been trying to remove the barrier between the races, so they appreciated Wuyan's actions.

Then, Wuyan, who shattered expectations wherever she went, fell in love with a man. Their union made her part of the imperial family, who were very reluctant to accept her into the fold.

Now a noble, Wuyan quickly donated the land of Jixia to Fuzi. Perhaps in some way, Jixia was like a home to her.

Like everything in her life, the stability and warmth of her married life did not endure for long. Her husband was killed in a Ferali ambush, and the loneliness that she had buried so deeply in her heart suddenly resurfaced. With nothing left for her in Yong, she returned to Jixia and began investigating the Feralis and their secrets. She wanted to know what happened to her beloved, to be informed of her ancestry, and to understand her powers.

Those who might seek to stop her would be wise to ponder if they can withstand a pounding from her colossal hammer.

The guild takes half of her earnings to repay the money they have invested in her, plus a little interest. She will be able to terminate her contract with them only after the debt is fully paid, at which point she can become a freelance mercenary, or pursue whatever other endeavor that might take her fancy.

lore:
Everyone has something beloved, and since nothing can be taken to the grave, everyone must suffer the pain of loss—be they the emperor of a civilization or a mere street orphan. That is why people inevitably turn to diviners, who claim to be able to foretell future fortunes and advise on all matters, just to ease their worries.

In the olden days, Taizong had been a wise ruler. At a time of great upheaval, his generals once led their cavalry to Alsahraa and recruited forces to resist the Feralis in the name of the Great Wall. Thus, the Great Wall Guardians were founded. Later, a fortress was built at the faraway Hero's Gorge, ushering in a period of peace to the Central Plains.

The queen sired three sons for Taizong. All three showed great merit, but the talented Prince Qian was selected and carefully groomed as the heir. Qian felt that his father favored his second son, however, which gave rise to a concealed yet ever-present anxiety. To protect his place as the heir to the throne, Qian sought out an oracle. The resulting divination foretold a foreboding future for Qian, which he was unwilling to accept. Furious, the prince ordered the oracle to be put to death. As the executioner's blade swept down, however, the mysterious oracle vanished into thin air, leaving behind only a single peony flower.

In the end, the wicked prince's plot was exposed. In a show of paternal clemency, Taizong only had him exiled. To protect the lives of all three of his beloved sons, he installed his magnanimous third son, the Prince of Jin. What was passed down through the following years were not only the praises of this prince-turned-emperor but also the legend of the Peony Diviner.

But all things change with time, and today, it is an empress who rules. Her Imperial Bureau of History, which revised the calendar system and presided over official rituals, recruited far and wide to enlist the most talented astronomers to observe the stars. The most skilled among them was a diviner peculiarly proficient at cultivating peonies, a man by the name of Ming. People whispered that Ming was a disciple of the legendary Peony Diviner, and when these whispers eventually reached the curious ears of the empress, she summoned him to court. Ming presented her with three trigrams, each predicting an upcoming battle for the Great Wall Guardians. Within a matter of days, all three predictions came true.

Ata was a new immigrant, and like many others, he was on the hunt for gold. To fulfill his dream, he willingly started to work in the city harbor.

An endless stream of traders and merchants stop in this city to rest and recharge, making it part of a prosperous trade route. Ata was strong and willing to endure hardships. He earned enough to not only meet his basic needs but also have some disposable income.

However, Ata's diligence became a threat in some people's eyes. Who told him to work this much? In due time, the laborers who relied on dock work for their livelihood—especially the elderly—would be starved by Ata's diligence.

As the kingdom had passed a series of policies to protect the rights and interests of immigrants, a group of tough, disgruntled men did not openly confront Ata, but instead quietly ambushed him in the alleyway he regularly passed through.

"You guys better not start any trouble!"

Facing this group of ruffians, Ata immediately greeted them with his fists.

Moments passed, and a black-and-blue-faced Ata finally came into an agreement with the ruffians sprawling messily on the floor. He came here to earn money and not to risk his life. Furthermore, after exchanging fists with these men, Ata developed a sense of camaraderie with them—indeed, the friendship between men is sometimes inexplicable.

And so just like that, the Ata who arrived alone and joined this group of misfits and took on all the jobs in the harbor. At the same time, he was also confident enough to negotiate a pay raise with the employers, thereby filling his money pouch to the fullest.

"These days are so... hic!"

lore:
"Without a great sage, this land would be doomed to darkness!"

Everyone in Primaera knows this saying. Even a three-year-old will tell you that the strongest person in the world is Fuzi. This is a legend, but also an unshakable belief.

Nobody knows how old the man is. They only know that, like a vast and rushing river, he has always been around.

Nor do they know how great his power is. They only know that, like a towering snowy mountain, the peak cannot be glimpsed.

There was once a sage named Jiang Ziya, whose power was comparable to that of Fuzi. At one time, they had been close companions.

Jiang Ziya had inherited the knowledge of antiquity and passed it down to his followers in the form of both mechanical arts and sorcery.

Fuzi, meanwhile, foresaw the potential dangers of this approach: The pursuit of the supreme, the root of knowledge of heaven and earth, was quite likely to cause students to lose all sense of fear, and thus stray from the path of life. Indeed, it was just such an unrestrained exploration of sorcery that caused so much destruction in ancient times, and which led to the creation of the feralis that posed such a grave threat to humanity and ultimately caused King Zhou's downfall.

Unwilling to accept Fuzi's advice, Jiang Ziya was bent on recreating the glory of antiquity. This disagreement eventually led to a complete severing of ties between the two great sages.

Later rulers agreed with Fuzi's view. In order to pass on valuable knowledge without bringing calamity upon the world, Fuzi founded an academy in Jixia, becoming the first of the "Three Sages of Jixia", alongside Zhuangzi and Mozi. Jixia Academy attracted the most gifted pupils from across the continent, teaching each according to their own talents and never treating any student differently based on their place of birth or clan affiliation. Over time, Jixia Academy became the epitome of higher learning in Primaera, a holy land for talented youths.

Chentang Pass is a mountain pass on the Eastern Sea, around which a city has gradually formed. Nezha grew up in Chentang Pass, where his father was a senior officer. He showed extraordinary talent from an early age: his strength, speed, and combat prowess far surpassed his peers, and even his older brothers were no match for him.

But Nezha had no friends. He found it hard to resist the urge to go berserk, which kept his peers at a distance. He only had one person, his mentor, on his side.

However, the mentor hid the truth from him: Nezha's heart had been replaced by a Wonder Key, whose power made Nezha extremely strong, but it also meant that he could feel no emotion besides anger.

The rulers of Celestia uncovered this secret and ordered Nezha's father to send him to Celestia as a hostage, and the mentor volunteered to accompany him. Celestia seemed like a bustling place to Nezha, but he also found it boring and stifling. Nezha couldn't help but annoy the people there, taking delight in their anger and helplessness. It was the only pleasure in his caged existence.

The people couldn't do anything to Nezha, so they decided to take out their revenge on the master. They reported him as a fugitive criminal and had him sent to jail. In a fit of rage at this injustice, Nezha escaped from Celestia.

As punishment for escaping, the rulers demanded that Nezha's father completely eradicate the feralis from the Eastern Sea. When Nezha returned to Chentang Pass, he found that storms and tidal waves had swept across the entire city, and the innocent citizens had been slaughtered by the enraged feralis. His hometown had been reduced to a vast expanse of water, having sacrificed itself to trap an enemy a hundred times stronger than itself.

lore:
As an orphan, Allain was fortunate enough to be taken in by the School of Steel and given the very best training. Unlike the other children, Allain displayed a fondness for swordplay, and given his immense talent, the instructors considered him a rising star.

"Remember, Allain: no matter what you want to do after you leave the School of Steel, use your sword to protect."

Keeping his instructor's words close to his heart, Allain began to picture his future as a skilled swordsman.

During his training, Allain met Butterfly, a blonde-haired fellow orphan. Allain was proud of his sword skills, but he proved to be no match for Butterfly. He began to develop inexplicable feelings for her: he wanted her to remain the strongest warrior she could be, but he also hoped to catch up with her so they could become a fearsome pair of blade-wielders. Over the following years of mutual support and growth, the two developed a profound bond.

Allain and Butterfly were sent on their first mission upon reaching the age of seventeen. Unaware that a traitor had sold them out, they walked straight into a Shadow Hand ambush. Seeking only to protect Butterfly, Allain dove headlong into the fray, but after the dust had settled, his body was nowhere to be found. By the time Allain reawakened, the Shadow Hand had transformed his body into human weaponry, erasing his memories and nullifying his emotions. All he knew was that the organization had given him a new life, a new blade, and a new mission—and for that simple reason, he was willing to serve them. During his missions, however, Allain was exposed to increasingly nefarious and disturbing things, and the unnerved Allain began to question his loyalty. The Shadow Hand discovered his reservations and planned to wipe his memories once again. Realizing that something was afoot, Allain decided to flee, but he was pursued by Shadow Hand assassins. Chased into dire straits, Allain fell into the sea and was never again seen in his homeland.

Whether by fate's mercy or mockery, Allain awoke in a shipping crate in Navenia's Vanilla Dock, unable to remember his prospective future, nor his time spent spilling blood for the sinister Shadow Hand. In the only fragment of memory he could bring to mind, he recalled a blonde-haired swordswoman protecting him, blocking countless flurries of blade slashes. As he fell into the sea, she was shouting at him: Allain. He surmised that this must be his name, but he remained puzzled at where his two swords had come from. Who was he? Where was he going? Allain didn't know, but he was determined to figure out why he wielded his swords.

The Three Sages of Jixia trained many talented disciples, and Sun Bin was one of the best.

Sun Bin was shy but gifted. His creativity uncovered a way to use machinery for warfare, and rulers were falling over each other in their eagerness to retain him. Despite being held in high regard, he remained humble and studious, winning the praise of the people.

But Sun Bin's talent also brought him disaster.

An older student became jealous of Sun Bin and repeatedly slandered him in front of others. Despite this, Sun Bin continued to treat him with the courtesy due to an elder. The onlookers became indignant, especially one of Sun Bin's friends, who repeatedly rebuked the older student for his behavior.

One fateful day, Sun Bin encountered a pack of raging Feralis on the way to some ruins near Jixia. While being chased by the creatures, he tumbled off a cliff and was buried in a ruin. When Sun Bin's friend realized he was missing, he went off in a frantic search. After making his way into the ruins and attempting to save Sun Bin, whose legs were gravely wounded, disaster struck. Some ancient machinery was triggered, causing ripples in the fabric of space-time. Sun Bin watched as his friend was sucked into a dark vortex, leaving behind only a stopped clock.

But this had been no accident—Sun Bin's jealous peer had planned the incident as revenge.

Yet fate had decided to spare the talented Sun Bin, as he was rescued by none other than the great master Mozi. His life was saved, albeit at the price of his legs and his best friend.

The shy youth became even more withdrawn. He immersed himself in machinery tomes day and night, and studied the mysteries of time. He carried the burden of his loss alone, and alone he held onto the conviction that he would find his friend.

While Sun Bin was immersed in his studies on the power of time, Jixia Academy held a great contest—the "Return of Dreams." An enthusiastic youth named Yao invited Sun Bin to join the "Team of Stars." Over the course of the contest, Sun Bin looked for ways to crack the mysteries of ancient machinery to find the answers he sought. However, he found nothing, and when it looked like the competition might require him to sacrifice his precious clock, he became visibly shaken.

Years ago, while still only a youth, Sima Yi set out from the city of Ye and headed to Jixia. Coming from a family of Anomalics, he often revisited his clan's past during his nightmares. Many of his ancestors had met their tragic ends because of a prophecy. Aside from inheriting these nightmares, he had also inherited exceptional abilities.

Sima Yi and Kongming were both top students at Jixia Academy. They admired each other's skills and became quick friends. They absorbed the wisdom of their sagely masters with impressive speed and were always eager to learn more. After consulting innumerable historical records, the duo departed Jixia. They left their footprints in ancient ruins, and all the way in the sandlands of the west. They were on the hunt for the origin of knowledge.

But Sima Yi's nightmares revealed that his friend would soon become an enemy. Sima Yi returned to Ye, where he was appointed strategist to Cao Cao, commander of the Wei army. At the same time, Kongming took a position as strategist for the Shu kingdom. Both young men had joined the struggle for the Three Kingdoms, but on opposite sides.

The former friends next met at the Battle of the Red Cliffs.

Kongming activated the Eastwind Altar, a powerful ancient artifact with tremendous killing power, dealing a devastating blow to the Ye fleet, which had been made up of Wei ships linked together with chains. A surging wave thrust Sima Yi's ship directly into the path of the artifact's blast.

As the pair crossed swords, Kongming questioned Sima Yi as to why their trust had been broken. "I do not wish to believe the world's prejudices against Anomalic clans, and yet, over the past years, you have aided Cao Cao as he wreaked havoc upon the Three Kingdoms, bringing endless war and suffering."

Sima Yi responded by recounting his own hardships and the truths he had learned from the origin of knowledge.

"Many years past, a prophecy from the origin of knowledge took the Three Kingdoms by storm. This prophecy was a curse upon the Anomalics, and my father died because of it."

"That's why I have spent years searching for the truth about the origin of knowledge—so that I can use its dark power to break the curse."

Countless pitch-black shadows swirled from Sima Yi's body.

lore:
"Many years ago, I walked past Kongming's hut many many times, always acting nonchalant. He always passed me by without even so much as a glance, but on the 180th time, he turned to me and spoke thus: 'Today, you meet your destiny.'"

"He emphasized that he was not a fortune teller, then walked away gracefully. A real character."

"I made my way toward the commandery inspector's place. This is a shameful story. The Heavenly Scrolls was a general term for any ancient texts that recorded secrets of mechcraft or sorcery. My ancestors once ruled over a kingdom, and when it was lost, they handed over their Heavenly Scrolls to a loyal minister for protection. It's a shame that I was so young and innocent. I made the mistake of trusting my former sworn brother Cao Cao, and told him of the scrolls at a banquet over some wine. Soon after, Cao Cao's army, who coveted the Heavenly Scrolls, invaded my homeland."

"The commandery inspector was the inside man then. To settle the matter with him, I began monitoring his movements under the guise of selling straw sandals."

"But on that day, something seemed very wrong. There was thick smoke billowing up from the mansion. Could it be a fire?"

"A crowd gathered in excitement, and amidst the chaos, an old man tore his shoes. I offered him a new pair and was just about to ask him about the situation, when he became overwhelmed with emotion and handed me a large package, before disappearing in an instant."

"A generous reward? No! It turned out to be a crying baby."

"A shadow fell and a guy holding a snake-like spear stared at me as if I... no, as if the child in my hands was his lifelong nemesis."

"'Hand it to me.' There was a strange, terrifying color to his eyes. It was pure hatred."

"I hugged the child closely. 'What do you want with my son?'"

"He let out a desolate laugh. 'No. This is the grandson of my sworn enemy.'"

"'No, this is my son. His name is Liu Shan, nicknamed A Dou. What, you want to check our ID?' I never knew I could embellish with such confidence."

Pei was once part of the Great Wall Guardians who guarded this majestic ancient miracle under the leadership of their senior officer, and he regarded it as his hometown.

Thousands of Feralis launched a fierce attack on the Great Wall. Fires burned through the pass, and it was a mix of howls from soldiers and warhorses. The guards were not strong enough, and the Great Wall was at risk of destruction.

Pei received an order to seek reinforcements. With his senior officer's letter in hand, he took the form of a tiger and charged out of the Feralis' encirclement. He dashed swiftly through the ancient road that led to Chang'an and sought help from the garrisons on the way. However, none believed the news of the attack on the Great Wall, and so they refused his request.

In a moment of desperation, Pei decided to rush to Chang'an on his own and deliver the letter. He stumbled through the bustling capital, but the guards refused him entry.

Pei displayed the letter to them: "Feralis have attacked the Great Wall! This was personally written by my senior officer..."

lore:
Dharma was born to subdue evil. At least, that's what the prophecies said.

A prince born beneath a majestic bodhi tree, Dharma was schooled in scriptures and martial arts by revered masters from a young age. He practiced asceticism religiously and helped the less fortunate, a mission he firmly committed to.

However, his homeland was soon torn apart. Traitors poisoned his father, and a black cloud of turmoil enveloped the kingdom. Blood soaked the ground as wails filled the air until finally, Dharma fell into deep despair. Though his fists were fearsome weapons, Dharma could not bring himself to harm his fellow countrymen. Thirsty for power, even his kin descended into reprehensible madness.

The leader of the traitors—one of Dharma's brothers—tried to pressure him by taking hostages. Dharma recognized the captives. They were orphans who the temple had taken in. The traitors demanded that he surrender the Royal Seal, or one orphan would be killed every fifteen minutes.

Dharma erupted in a fury. Losing all control, nearly half the palace was pulverized beneath his fists—traitors included. However, in the wake of such devastation, the kingdom became unsalvageable.

Even worse, unaware that Dharma had eradicated the evil, survivors blamed him for the catastrophe and banished him, slinging curses at him all the while.

Dharma did not defend himself but was instead filled with deep regret. The bright eyes of those frightened orphans—and their will to survive—would forever remain etched in his mind.

Before long, those eyes became thorns in his heart, tormenting his every waking moment. Self-exiled, he wandered without direction or destination until he collapsed in despair under the scorching sun. Vultures circled above, waiting to feed on his remains.

lore:
Guan Yu was one of the strongest demon hunters in the world. He carried a sword called Soaring Green Dragon, which he had won in a battle with ancient Feralis. The battle cost the lives of dozens of his fellow hunters, so Guan Yu treasured the sword as much as he did his brethren. In a world where Feralis run rampant, even the poorest villages had to scrape together enough money to purchase the services of demon hunters.

One day, a client approached Guan Yu with a request to drive off a human-ferali hybrid. Unwilling to harm a hybrid, Guan Yu refused the assignment. The stubborn client, however, asked to borrow Guan Yu's sword, saying, "Those ferali hybrids are machinists. Who knows how many weapons of destruction they've created? Do you value your sword more than you value human life?" Ever arrogant, Guan Yu was angered. Confident that no one would dare trick him, he loaned out his sword.

The Soaring Green Dragon was returned not long after, but a bounty had been put out on Guan Yu's head. An entire human village had been slaughtered, and all the survivors agreed that the killer's weapon had been the Soaring Green Dragon. Everyone knew who owned that weapon. In a single night, the hunter had become the hunted.

Guan Yu was enraged at having been used and his reputation tarnished. The killer had even sullied the names of his comrades who had given their lives for the sword. Was this a plot by his Ferali enemies? Guan Yu decided to face the hybrid feralis head-on.

lore:
The dream eaters are fantastical creatures birthed by heaven and earth. They can enter the dreamscapes of other organisms and eat dreams for sustenance. They live far from the realm of humans in the Forest of Dreams. Only when they have grown to maturity do they set out in search of dreams on which to feast.

On the day of his coming of age ceremony, a young dream eater came to the human world. To fill his rumbling belly, he traversed a multitude of dreams and experienced countless wonders. Fearless, the dream eater even dared sneaking into a place where the superbeings were holding sacred meetings, hiding in an inconspicuous corner and waiting for his chance to munch on their delicious dreams.

However, the superbeings continued with their discussions for days on end, stopping not once to take a rest. Eventually, one of them grew weary of the long meeting. His eyes began to droop, and he soon dozed off. The dream eater had been waiting for this moment and pounced into his dreams.

And what a dream! This was much more magnificent than anything he had encountered before. Floating cities, humans on flying ships, and a blizzard that engulfed it all... The dream eater wandered about for so long that he forgot to leave.

The superbeing sensed the dream eater's presence and grabbed his tail. Frightened, he tried to burrow deeper into the dream. The superbeing laughed and asked, "From where do you come? And where are you going?"

"Can't speak, eh? An eater of dreams... let's call you Menki, shall we?"

lore:
The Misty Marshes was one of the most mysterious areas of Primaera. A great river flowed through forests, swamps, and ancient ruins. The worship of ancient rulers could still be found there, and the power to interpret the faith belonged to the Omniscients. They used this power and the "Wonder" to rule over the people here.

As time went on, the Omniscients weakened because they were unable to adapt to the changing times. The order they established began to falter, and heretics started appearing among the devout people of the Riverlands.

Liu Bang was one such heretic. He had little patience for faith, and preferred gold over religion. To him, the end justified the means.

He did everything he could to eventually become a minor civil servant, but he quickly realized that what he got in return was not satisfactory. His superiors used him, but they were also wary of him. He was no fool, and eventually a bold idea came to mind. The Omniscients needed to perform rituals to display the ancient powers that only they could wield. If he somehow managed to perform the "Wonder," could he take their place and become the ruler of the land? The idea enthralled him.

But he would not have come up with it if it weren't for Liang, who, despite having mastered Power Word, didn't know the first thing about survival. He was causing trouble wherever he went, and couldn't even guarantee his next meal. Liu Bang helped him out and gained his trust, then easily convinced Liang to take him to the marshlands where the Omniscients performed their Wonder.

Liang was also curious about the Wonder.

Using Power Word, they charmed the guard and were able to witness the ritual. The nine Omniscients—and the two trespassers—were bathed in the blinding light of the Wonder as the Omniscients chanted. Liang spoke to the Wonder with his power, and the conversation proved that Ziya's predictions were true, including... the fate of the Dark Master...

When the Omniscients took off their masks, Liu Bang was surprised to find that the rulers of the Riverlands were not humans, but monsters!

lore:
For a long time, legends of a Heavenly Tree have been told in the Misty Marshes. They reached the ears of a scholar, Guiguzi, who grew curious about the legend.

A simple man, he had an interest in all natural phenomena. So, he set off into the depths of the marshes alone, in search of the roots of that tree.

He found something strange—a dazzling light emanating from inside the tree. When he awoke, he discovered his appearance had changed. It was as if time had turned back and made him young again.

Any other resident of the forest would have been terrified or angered. But Guiguzi was excited and fascinated. He was mesmerized by this strange light. He swore to dedicate his life to discovering the truth behind the mystery. When he went back to the surface, he discovered disaster had struck the forest. The Sky Dome was shattered, and the forest ravaged by war. To protect the Sky Dome, the nine Seers had disappeared into the mist. The Order of the Seers took over the mission of protecting the Sky Dome and the Heavenly Tree.

To continue his research, Guiguzi joined the Order of the Seers, where he learned of the Wonder they concealed.

He was baffled by the fragments of the past he saw within the Wonder... Shattered statues, a desolate ravine, and a scorched land covered by the Sky Dome. Nothing he saw matched up with what he already knew. But from amidst it all he made out a mysterious voice: nature's whisper.

It seemed like sorcery, yet it was not. It was so faint it could barely be heard, yet still pure and profound.

Guiguzi told himself that he still lacked knowledge. Amidst his doubts, he then threw himself into his research. After many years, he became an erudite scholar, known for his knowledge and wisdom. When the Order of the Seers founded their school, his understanding and passion for the natural world made him the most popular of all the teachers.

lore:
Xuance would never forget that day, the day a hoard of brigands attacked their border town. The Great Wall Guard and the townspeople did their best to defend the city gates. The brigands who were trapped inside the town took the elderly and the weak as hostages to make their escape.

A moment of utter terror. Yet the cries of the townsfolk broke the young man's heart. He climbed out of the water tank in which he was hiding and ran over to help.

He doesn't remember much after that, only that the bad guys weren't your average brigands, and that they all ended up dying at the hand of their leader. His older brother never came to his aid, no one did. Xuance was chosen by the leader to be sacrificed in order to awaken something powerful. Amid the fleeing crowd and chaos, desperate and fearful, Xuance watched in horror as a nameless swordsman was engulfed in an evil mist in his stead.

Once everything fell quiet, and the full moon silently illuminated the vast desert, the man took him away.

From that day on, Xuance took Prince of Lanling as his master, and they lived by the nearly dried-up Mooneye Sea. After years of brutal training, Xuance grew into a skilled nightwalker with a sickle as his only companion.

The Prince of Lanling lived in seclusion, gathering intel from his former subordinates, and disappearing and returning from time to time. He didn't trust a soul, and always acted alone. In his signature style, the little madman was accustomed to stirring up trouble all by himself as he wandered the desert.

The survivors of the disaster had been scattered across the desert, struggling to survive in the harsh elements and under the constant threat of the feralis. But wherever people gather, oppression and strife will always follow.

The little madman was the nemesis of injustice. At first, he only challenged feralis stronger than himself, but quickly he learned how to shuttle back and forth between different oases in the desert, harassing and combating any who might use their power to toy with the fates of others: crooked brigands, tyrannical nomad leaders, hustlers traveling the Silk Road, and plain old scoundrels in search of power. This mad pleasure was a means of catharsis for his pain, allowing him to exact revenge on those who orchestrated the trauma of his past.

lore:
Ever heard of ghosts?

A ghost wandered the dense forest—a forest that held the remains of an ancient deity. Patrolling the lands of the past, the ghost punished all who entered its forbidden domain.

However, the most outstanding female warrior of the Knights of the Round Table was determined to fight the ghost of the Forbidden Realm.

Born into a clan of acclaimed knights, it was in her blood to guard Eventide Cathedral with fervent faith.

One month ago, she encountered the ghost while on night patrol.

Her martial instincts were provoked as soon as she set eyes on the ghost, causing her to draw her sword. While she was confident in her talent, her opponent was equally skilled in combat. Its spear smashed into her sword, sending her reeling. As her natural thirst for victory kicked in, she forgot all about her patrol, and the danger, desiring only to defeat her enemy with strength and skill!

And that is precisely what she did.

Illuminated by moonlight, the duel drew to a close as the ghost was vanquished. In the next moment, she witnessed an extraordinary phenomenon: a new glory descending, an incomparable radiance upon the Eventide Cathedral!

From that night on, the knight began having vivid and recurrent nightmares. Her passion for fighting, too, was enhanced even more than before—a desire to win, a desire to regain the brilliant glory of the past. When morning arrived, she always found herself gripping her blade, ready to fight at a moment's notice.

To banish the nightmares, the knight tried staying up all night training, but she still heard voices calling. The voices spoke some ancient language in unintelligible mutterings—yet somehow in perfect rhythm with her heartbeat.

Fight! Fight! Fight! For the glory of Eventide Cathedral! It was as if her body contained another self, a self that told her what her true mission was.

Were these the memories of the ghost? Pride, resignation, beckoning... Within her heart surged a powerful yearning to learn everything about this land.

lore:
Merlyn was "once" one of the most mysterious mages on the continent. She bore a great mission—to assist the King and revive Eventide Cathedral.

Regrettably, "once" is the key word... because she'd made a grave mistake. That's right—she made a mistake when using a spell and accidentally trapped herself in a bubble cage! A cage which hung high on a big, old tree.

No one knew how many years passed in that bubble. She racked her brains to break out, but could do nothing more than throw her gadgets out of it while she stayed trapped inside. One day, she saw the child of a hunter passing by and inspiration came to her—to create an irresistible doll and throw it under the tree!

Soon, the little girl Angela found the doll. She picked it up and adored it right away. At that moment, the spell on the doll took effect. Soul Exchange!

Success! Merlyn could now leave the cage and enter the body of the little girl. But... she felt a little strange. Merlyn couldn't care less and wanted to leave the forest with her newfound body, so she cast a pathfinding spell. Perhaps she was concentrating too hard... but she never noticed the hand gently resting on her shoulder.

It was a kind-hearted paladin who had found the lost girl and wanted to take her home.

In an instant, Merlyn knew what the problem was. As soon as she saw him, she couldn't take her eyes off him, and her feet couldn't help but follow and do whatever he said with complete obedience.

This body must have always admired the paladin, and the admiration was so strong that Merlyn was unable to resist it.

Merlyn grew frantic. She didn't leave the cage just to fall in love with a frail human! She decided to get rid of him as soon as she returned to town.

Fortunately, the first passerby they met greeted the paladin and called him "Arthur."

Immediately, unpleasant memories of her dark history came flooding into the mind of the little girl. Merlyn... Oh wait, Angela now. Yes, she was known as the world's greatest and most righteous mage, but it was all a facade. In fact, she was just a loser. She was a genius who originally wanted to take over the world, but was cursed by fate to serve King Arthur, and was forced to assist in the revival of Eventide Cathedral.

Eventide Cathedral?! She was going to destroy it! She thought she was finally free after King Arthur's death, only to be trapped again by another mistake.
